title.zh: 卷二百上 列傳第一百五十上: 安祿山 高尚 孫孝哲 史思明
title.en: Volume 200 Biographies 150: An Lushan, Gao Shang, Sun Xiaozhe, Shi Siming
title.raw: 卷二百上 列傳第一百五十上: 安祿山 高尚 孫孝哲 史思明 Volume 200 Biographies 150: An Lushan, Gao Shang, Sun Xiaozhe, Shi Siming

sentences.zh: 安祿山子慶緒 高尚 孫孝哲 史思明子朝義

translations.literal: An Lushan's son Qingxu; Gao Shang; Sun Xiaozhe; Shi Siming's son Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan's son Qingxu; Gao Shang; Sun Xiaozhe; and Shi Siming's son Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 安祿山，營州柳城雜種胡人也，本無姓氏，名軋犖山。

translations.literal: An Lushan was a man of mixed Hu descent from Liucheng in Ying Prefecture. He originally had no surname; his name was Yalushan.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan came from Liucheng in Ying Prefecture, a frontier town of mixed Hu peoples. He had no family name at birth and was called Yalushan.

sentences.zh: 母阿史德氏，亦突厥巫師，以卜為業。

translations.literal: His mother was of the Ashide clan; she too was a Türk shaman who made her living by divination.
translations.idiomatic: His mother belonged to the Ashide clan and was likewise a Türk shaman who earned her living through divination.

sentences.zh: 突厥呼鬥戰為軋犖山，遂以名之。

translations.literal: The Türks called fighting douzhan "yalushan," and so he was given that name.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Türks, fighting was called yalushan, and this became his name.

sentences.zh: 少孤，隨母在突厥中，將軍安波至兄延偃妻其母。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he followed his mother among the Türks. When General An Bo arrived, his elder brother Yan Yan married his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father early and grew up with his mother among the Türks. Later General An Bo came, and Yan Yan, the elder brother of An Bo, took his mother as wife.

sentences.zh: 開元初，與將軍安道買男俱逃出突厥中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era, he fled from among the Türks together with the son of General An Daomai.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan years he escaped from the Türk lands together with the son of General An Daomai.

sentences.zh: 道買次男貞節為嵐州別駕，收穫之。

translations.literal: Daomai's second son Zhenjie was assistant prefect of Lan Prefecture and took them in.
translations.idiomatic: Daomai's second son Zhenjie, then assistant prefect of Lan Prefecture, received and sheltered them.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，以與其兄及延偃相攜而出，感愧之，約與思順等並為兄弟，冒姓為安。

translations.literal: When he was just over ten, having come out together with his brother and Yan Yan, he was moved to gratitude; he agreed with them and Sishun and the others to become sworn brothers and assumed the surname An.
translations.idiomatic: Still in his early teens, he had left the Türks with his brother and Yan Yan; deeply moved by their kindness, he swore brotherhood with them and with Sishun and the rest, and took the surname An.

sentences.zh: 及長，解六蕃語，為互市牙郎。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he mastered the six foreign languages and became a broker for frontier trade.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he learned six frontier languages and served as a trade broker at the border markets.

sentences.zh: 二十年，張守珪為幽州節度，祿山盜羊事覺，守珪剝坐，欲棒殺之，大呼曰：「大夫不欲滅兩蕃耶？

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Zhang Shougui was military commissioner of Youzhou. An Lushan's theft of sheep was discovered. Shougui stripped him and seated him for beating, intending to club him to death. An Lushan shouted: "Does the Grand Marshal not wish to destroy both foreign realms?
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Kaiyuan, Zhang Shougui held Youzhou as military commissioner. When An Lushan's sheep theft came to light, Shougui had him stripped and bound for beating and was about to club him to death. An Lushan cried out: "Grand Marshal, do you not mean to destroy both the Khitan and the Xi?

sentences.zh: 何為打殺祿山！」

translations.literal: Why beat Lushan to death!"
translations.idiomatic: Why kill Lushan!"

sentences.zh: 守珪見其肥白，壯其言而釋之。

translations.literal: Shougui saw how fat and fair-skinned he was, was impressed by his words, and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui saw his stout, fair complexion, was struck by his bold speech, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 令與鄉人史思明同捉生，行必克獲，拔為偏將。

translations.literal: He had him capture living prisoners together with his fellow townsman Shi Siming; they always succeeded on campaign and were promoted to deputy generals.
translations.idiomatic: He paired him with his townsman Shi Siming to take captives on raids; they never failed, and both were raised to deputy general.

sentences.zh: 常嫌其肥，以守珪威風素高，畏懼不敢飽食。

translations.literal: He was always troubled by his fatness; because Shougui's authority was so formidable, he feared to eat his fill.
translations.idiomatic: He was forever self-conscious about his weight; Shougui's stern reputation was so great that he dared not eat his fill.

sentences.zh: 以驍勇聞，遂養為子。

translations.literal: His fierce bravery became known, and Shougui adopted him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: When his valor became famous, Shougui adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，為平盧兵馬使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was made military commissioner of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he became Pinglu's army commander.

sentences.zh: 性巧黠，人多譽之。

translations.literal: He was crafty and clever; many people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and quick-witted, he won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 授營州都督、平盧軍使。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Ying Prefecture and commissioner of the Pinglu army.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as governor of Ying Prefecture and commissioner of the Pinglu army.

sentences.zh: 厚賂往來者，乞為好言，玄宗益信響之。

translations.literal: He lavishly bribed those who traveled to and fro to beg good words on his behalf; Emperor Xuanzong came to trust him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He paid lavish bribes to every traveler passing through, asking them to speak well of him, and Xuanzong's confidence in him only grew.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，以平盧為節度，以祿山攝中丞為使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, Pinglu became a circuit, with Lushan serving as deputy commissioner in charge of the commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Tianbao year Pinglu was made a frontier circuit, and Lushan was named its commissioner while holding the post of deputy censor.

sentences.zh: 入朝奏事，玄宗益寵之。

translations.literal: When he entered court to report, Xuanzong favored him still more.
translations.idiomatic: On his visits to court to report affairs, Xuanzong showered him with still greater favor.

sentences.zh: 三載，代裴寬為范陽節度，河北採訪、平盧軍等使如故。

translations.literal: In the third year he replaced Pei Kuan as commissioner of Fanyang, retaining his posts as Hebei surveillance commissioner and Pinglu army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he succeeded Pei Kuan as Fanyang commissioner while keeping his Hebei surveillance and Pinglu army commands.

sentences.zh: 採訪使張利貞常受其賂；

translations.literal: The surveillance commissioner Zhang Lizhen regularly received his bribes;
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance commissioner Zhang Lizhen was regularly in his pay;

sentences.zh: 數載之後，黜陟使席建侯又言其公直無私；

translations.literal: several years later the promotion-and-demotion commissioner Xi Jianhou again spoke of his fairness and lack of private interest;
translations.idiomatic: and a few years later the promotion commissioner Xi Jianhou likewise praised his impartiality;

sentences.zh: 裴寬受代，及李林甫順旨，並言其美。

translations.literal: when Pei Kuan was replaced, and Li Linfu toed the imperial line—all spoke of his virtues.
translations.idiomatic: when Pei Kuan left office and Li Linfu chimed with the throne—all alike extolled his merits.

sentences.zh: 數公皆信臣，玄宗意益堅不搖矣。

translations.literal: These several men were all trusted ministers; Xuanzong's mind grew ever firmer and unshaken.
translations.idiomatic: These men were all trusted officials, and the emperor's confidence in him became unshakable.

sentences.zh: 後請為貴妃養兒，入對皆先拜太真。

translations.literal: Later he asked to become the Noble Consort's adopted son; whenever he entered audience he would first bow to Taizhen.
translations.idiomatic: He later asked to be adopted as the Noble Consort's son, and at every audience he bowed first to Lady Yang.

sentences.zh: 玄宗怪而問之，對曰：「臣是蕃人，蕃人先母而後父。」

translations.literal: Xuanzong wondered at this and questioned him. He replied: "Your servant is a barbarian; among barbarians one honors the mother before the father."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong was puzzled and asked why. He answered: "I am a frontier man, and among us one honors the mother before the father."

sentences.zh: 玄宗大悅，遂命楊銛已下並約為兄弟姊妹。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was greatly pleased and ordered Yang Xian and those below to swear brotherhood and sisterhood with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and had Yang Xian and the rest of the clan bind themselves to him as sworn kin.

sentences.zh: 六載，加大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was raised to Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 常令劉駱穀奏事。

translations.literal: He regularly had Liu Luogu report affairs to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He routinely sent Liu Luogu to court with his reports.

sentences.zh: 與王鉷俱為大夫。

translations.literal: He and Wang Hong were both Grand Counselors.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wang Hong both held the rank of Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 李林甫為相，朝臣莫敢抗禮，祿山承恩深。

translations.literal: When Li Linfu was chief minister, no courtier dared stand against his precedence; Lushan enjoyed deep favor.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Linfu as chief minister, no courtier dared withhold full obeisance—yet Lushan, so deeply favored, did not.

sentences.zh: 入謁不甚罄折。

translations.literal: When he entered audience he did not bow very deeply.
translations.idiomatic: On audience days his bows were perfunctory.

sentences.zh: 林甫命王鉷，鉷趨拜謹甚，祿山悚息，腰漸曲。

translations.literal: Linfu summoned Wang Hong; Hong hurried forward and bowed with great care. Lushan trembled and held his breath, his waist gradually bending.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu would call Wang Hong forward; Hong would rush to bow with meticulous deference, while Lushan, quaking, slowly bent his waist.

sentences.zh: 每與語，皆揣知其情而先言之。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke with Lushan, he would divine his feelings and speak of them first.
translations.idiomatic: In every conversation he seemed to read Lushan's mind and voice it before Lushan could.

sentences.zh: 祿山以為神明，每見林甫，雖盛冬亦汗洽。

translations.literal: Lushan took him for a spirit; whenever he saw Linfu, even in deep winter he would sweat profusely.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan regarded him as uncanny; even in midwinter he broke into a sweat at the sight of him.

sentences.zh: 林甫接以溫言，中書廳引坐，以己披袍覆之，祿山欣荷，無所隱，呼為十郎。

translations.literal: Linfu received him with warm words, had him seated in the Secretariat hall, and covered him with his own loose robe. Lushan was overjoyed and hid nothing, calling him Tenth Son.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu would greet him kindly, seat him in the Secretariat, and drape his own robe over him. Grateful and unguarded, Lushan called him "Tenth Son."

sentences.zh: 駱穀奏事，先問：「十郎何言？」

translations.literal: When Luogu reported affairs, Lushan would first ask: "What did Tenth Son say?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Luogu brought word from court, Lushan would ask first: "What did Tenth Son say?"

sentences.zh: 有好言則喜躍，若但言「大夫須好檢校」，則反手據床曰：「阿與，我死也！」

translations.literal: If the words were favorable he would leap for joy; if it was only "The Grand Marshal must keep a close check," he would slap the bed and cry: "Ayu! I'm done for!"
translations.idiomatic: Good news sent him leaping with delight; if the message was only "The Grand Marshal must keep close watch," he would slap the bed and wail, "Ayu, I'm finished!"

sentences.zh: 李龜年嘗敩其說，玄宗以為笑樂。

translations.literal: Li Guinian once repeated this story, and Xuanzong found it hilarious.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guinian once mimicked this for the emperor, who laughed with delight.

sentences.zh: 晚年益肥壯，腹垂過膝，重三百三十斤，每行以肩膊左右抬挽其身，方能移步。

translations.literal: In his later years he grew ever stouter; his belly hung past his knees. He weighed three hundred thirty jin; whenever he walked, attendants on left and right had to lift his shoulders and arms before he could move.
translations.idiomatic: In later life he grew immense: his belly hung below his knees, and he weighed three hundred thirty jin. To walk at all he needed men on either side hoisting his shoulders.

sentences.zh: 至玄宗前，作胡旋舞，疾如風焉。

translations.literal: Before Xuanzong he would perform the Hu whirling dance, swift as the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet before the emperor he would whirl in the Hu spin-dance, quick as wind.

sentences.zh: 為置第宇，窮極壯麗，以金銀為篣筐笊籬等。

translations.literal: A mansion was built for him, magnificence pushed to the limit; even baskets, scoops, and strainers were made of gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: The court built him a residence of staggering splendor, with baskets and kitchen tools wrought in gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 上御勤政樓，於御坐東為設一大金雞障，前置一榻坐之，卷去其簾。

translations.literal: When the emperor attended the Qinzheng Tower, a great golden rooster screen was set up east of the imperial seat; a couch was placed before it for Lushan to sit, and the curtain was rolled away.
translations.idiomatic: At the Qinzheng Tower the emperor had a great golden rooster screen set east of his seat, with a couch before it where Lushan sat in full view, the curtain drawn back.

sentences.zh: 十載入朝，又求為河東節度，因拜之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he entered court and again asked for the Hedong commission; the appointment was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On his tenth-year audience he sought and received the Hedong commission as well.

sentences.zh: 男十一人：長子慶宗，太僕卿，少子慶緒，鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons: the eldest Qingzong was Minister of the Stud; the youngest Qingxu was Minister of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Of his eleven sons, the eldest Qingzong was Minister of the Stud and the youngest Qingxu Minister of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 慶宗又尚郡主。

translations.literal: Qingzong also married a commandery princess.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzong had moreover married an imperial commandery princess.

sentences.zh: 祿山陰有逆謀，于范陽北築雄武城，外示禦寇，內貯兵器，積穀為保守之計，戰馬萬五千匹，牛羊稱是。

translations.literal: Lushan secretly harbored a plan of rebellion. North of Fanyang he built Xiongwu Fort, outwardly to repel raiders but inwardly to store weapons and grain for a defensive scheme—fifteen thousand war horses and livestock in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly plotting rebellion, he built Xiongwu Fort north of Fanyang, ostensibly against raiders but in truth to stock arms and grain for a stand: fifteen thousand war horses and herds to match.

sentences.zh: 兼三道節度，進奏無不允。

translations.literal: Holding all three frontier commissions, none of his memorials was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Commanding three circuits, he obtained every request he sent up.

sentences.zh: 引張通儒、李庭堅、平冽、李史魚、獨孤問俗在幕下，高尚掌書記，劉駱谷留居西京為耳目，安守忠、李歸仁、蔡希德、牛庭玠、向潤客、崔乾祐、尹子奇、何千年、武令珣、能元皓、田承嗣、田乾真，皆拔於行間。

translations.literal: He brought Zhang Tongru, Li Tingjian, Ping Lie, Li Shiyu, and Dugu Wensu onto his staff; Gao Shang kept the secretariat; Liu Luogu remained in the western capital as his eyes and ears. An Shouzhong, Li Guiren, Cai Xide, Niu Tingjie, Xiang Runke, Cui Qianyou, Yin Ziqi, He Qiannian, Wu Lingxun, Neng Yuanhao, Tian Chengsi, and Tian Qianzhen were all promoted from the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tongru, Li Tingjian, Ping Lie, Li Shiyu, and Dugu Wensu served on his staff; Gao Shang ran his secretariat; Liu Luogu stayed in Chang'an as his informant. An Shouzhong, Li Guiren, Cai Xide, Niu Tingjie, Xiang Runke, Cui Qianyou, Yin Ziqi, He Qiannian, Wu Lingxun, Neng Yuanhao, Tian Chengsi, and Tian Qianzhen were all men he had plucked from the ranks.

sentences.zh: 每月進奉生口駝馬鷹犬不絕，人無聊矣。

translations.literal: Every month he sent tribute without cease—captives, camels, horses, hawks, and hounds—and the people were worn out.
translations.idiomatic: Month after month he flooded the court with captives, camels, horses, hawks, and hounds until the realm groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 既肥大不任戰，前後十餘度欺誘契丹，宴設酒中著莨菪子，預掘一坑，待其昏醉，斬首埋之，皆不覺死，每度數十人。

translations.literal: Now too fat for battle, more than ten times he deceived and lured Khitan guests: at banquets he put datura seeds in the wine, had a pit dug beforehand, and when they fell drunk he beheaded them and buried them—they never knew they were dying; each time several dozen men.
translations.idiomatic: Too corpulent to fight, he more than ten times tricked Khitan envoys: at feasts he drugged their wine with datura, had pits dug in advance, and when they collapsed drunk he beheaded and buried them unawares—dozens each time.

sentences.zh: 十一載八月，祿山並率河東等軍五六萬，號十五萬，以討契丹。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eleventh year, Lushan jointly led fifty or sixty thousand troops from Hedong and elsewhere, claiming one hundred fifty thousand, to attack the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the eleventh year he marched with fifty or sixty thousand men from Hedong and allied commands—claiming a hundred fifty thousand—to chastise the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 去平盧千餘里，至土護真河，即北黃河也。

translations.literal: More than a thousand li from Pinglu, they reached the Tuhu'er River—the northern Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand li beyond Pinglu they reached the Tuhu'er River, the northern branch of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 又倍程三百里，奄至契丹牙帳。

translations.literal: They doubled the pace another three hundred li and suddenly arrived at the Khitan royal encampment.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed another three hundred li at double speed and fell suddenly on the Khitan royal camp.

sentences.zh: 屬久雨，弓箭皆漲濕，將士困極，奚又夾攻之，殺傷略盡。

translations.literal: It had rained for a long time; bows and arrows were swollen and sodden, and the troops were utterly exhausted. The Xi attacked from both flanks as well, and casualties were nearly total.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged rain had soaked every bow; the army was spent. The Xi struck from both sides, and the force was all but annihilated.

sentences.zh: 祿山被射，折其玉簪，以麾下奚小兒二十餘人走上山，墜坑中，其男慶緒等扶持之。

translations.literal: Lushan was struck by an arrow that broke his jade hairpin. With more than twenty Xi youths from his retinue he fled up a mountain, fell into a pit, and was supported out by his son Qingxu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow struck Lushan and snapped his jade hairpin. He fled up a hill with twenty-odd Xi boys from his escort, tumbled into a pit, and was hauled out by Qingxu and his sons.

sentences.zh: 會夜，解走，投平盧城。

translations.literal: When night came they broke away and fled, reaching Pinglu city.
translations.idiomatic: Under cover of night they escaped and made for Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠屢奏祿山必反。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong repeatedly memorialized that Lushan would surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong repeatedly warned the throne that Lushan would rebel.

sentences.zh: 十二載，玄宗使中官輔璆琳覘之，得其賄賂，盛言其忠。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Xuanzong sent the eunuch Fu Yuolin to observe him; Yuolin received his bribes and spoke at length of his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the emperor sent the eunuch Fu Yuolin to spy on him; Yuolin took Lushan's bribes and returned praising his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 國忠又云「召必不至」，洎召之而至。

translations.literal: Guozhong also said, "If summoned he will surely not come"—yet when he was summoned, he came.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong had said, "Summon him and he will not come"—yet when summoned, he came.

sentences.zh: 十三載正月，謁于華清宮，因涕泣言：「臣蕃人，不識字，陛下擢臣不次，被楊國忠欲得殺臣。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year he had audience at Huaqing Palace and, weeping, said: "Your servant is a barbarian and cannot read. Your Majesty raised me out of turn, and now Yang Guozhong seeks to have me killed."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year he appeared at Huaqing Palace and wept: "I am an illiterate frontier man whom Your Majesty raised beyond merit, and Yang Guozhong now wants me dead."

sentences.zh: 玄宗益親厚之，遂以為左僕射，卻回。

translations.literal: Xuanzong treated him with still greater intimacy and warmth, made him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drew him closer still, named him Left Vice Director, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 其月，又請為閑廄、隴右群牧等都使，奏吉溫為武部侍郎、兼中丞，為其副，又請知總監事。

translations.literal: That same month he again asked to be commissioner of the Imperial Stud, Longyou herd-masters, and related offices; he memorialized Ji Wen as Vice Minister of War and concurrent censor as his deputy, and also asked to supervise the directorate overall.
translations.idiomatic: That month he also sought command of the imperial studs and Longyou pastures, named Ji Wen his deputy as vice minister and censor, and asked overall supervision of the directorate.

sentences.zh: 既為閑廄、群牧等使，上筋腳馬，皆陰選擇之，奪得樓煩監牧及奪張文儼馬牧。

translations.literal: Once he was commissioner of the Stud and herd-masters, he secretly selected the finest horses presented to the throne and seized the Loufan stud and Zhang Wenyian's pastures.
translations.idiomatic: As stud commissioner he secretly culled the best tribute horses and seized the Loufan stud and Zhang Wenyian's pastures.

sentences.zh: 三月一日，歸范陽，疾行出關，日行三四百里，至范陽，人言反者，玄宗必大怒，縛送與之。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month he returned to Fanyang, marching out of the pass at forced speed—three or four hundred li a day. When he reached Fanyang, anyone who spoke of rebellion was seized by Xuanzong in great anger and bound and sent to Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the third month he raced from the capital at three or four hundred li a day. At Fanyang, anyone who called him a rebel was, by imperial order, bound and delivered to him.

sentences.zh: 十四載，玄宗又召之，托疾不至。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Xuanzong summoned him again; he pleaded illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the emperor summoned him again; he pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 賜其子婚，令就觀禮，又辭。

translations.literal: The emperor granted his son a marriage and ordered him to attend the ceremony; he declined again.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted his son a royal marriage and bade him attend; he declined once more.

sentences.zh: 十一月，反于范陽，矯稱奉恩命以兵討逆賊楊國忠。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he rebelled at Fanyang, falsely claiming he had received an imperial grace-command to take troops and punish the traitor Yang Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he rose at Fanyang, claiming an imperial mandate to march against the traitor Yang Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 以諸蕃馬步十五萬，夜半行，平明食，日六十里。

translations.literal: With one hundred fifty thousand cavalry and infantry from the various barbarian peoples, they marched at night, ate at dawn, and covered sixty li a day.
translations.idiomatic: He led a hundred fifty thousand barbarian horse and foot, marching by night, eating at dawn, sixty li a day.

sentences.zh: 以高尚、嚴莊為謀主，孫孝哲、高邈、何千年為腹心。

translations.literal: Gao Shang and Yan Zhuang were his chief strategists; Sun Xiaozhe, Gao Miao, and He Qiannian were his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shang and Yan Zhuang plotted for him; Sun Xiaozhe, Gao Miao, and He Qiannian were his trusted confidants.

sentences.zh: 天下承平日久，人不知戰，聞其兵起，朝廷震驚。

translations.literal: The realm had been at peace so long that people knew nothing of war; when they heard his armies had risen, the court was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had lasted so long that war was unimaginable; at news of his revolt the court reeled.

sentences.zh: 禁衛皆市井商販之人，乃開左藏庫出錦帛召募。

translations.literal: The palace guards were all men of the market stalls and shops; the left treasury was opened and silks and cloth issued to recruit troops.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guard were shopkeepers and peddlers; the left treasury was opened and silks paid out to raise men.

sentences.zh: 因以高仙芝、封常清等相次為大將以擊之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gao Xianzhi, Feng Changqing, and others were appointed in succession as grand generals to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianzhi, Feng Changqing, and others were sent in turn as supreme commanders against him.

sentences.zh: 祿山令嚴肅，得士死力，無不一當百，遇之必敗。

translations.literal: Lushan's orders were strict; he won men's utmost effort in death. None failed to fight one as a hundred; whoever met them was sure to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan's discipline was iron; his men fought as if each were worth a hundred, and every clash went his way.

sentences.zh: 十二月，度河至陳留郡，河南節度張介然城陷死之，傳首河北。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he crossed the river to Chenliu Commandery. Zhang Jieran, military commissioner of Henan, died when the city fell; his head was sent through Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he crossed into Chenliu; Henan commissioner Zhang Jieran died in the fall of the city, and his head was paraded through Hebei.

sentences.zh: 陳留郭門祿山男慶緒見誅慶宗榜，泣告祿山，祿山在輿中驚哭曰：「吾子何罪而殺之！」

translations.literal: At the outer gate of Chenliu, Lushan's son Qingxu saw the placard announcing Qingzong's execution and, weeping, told Lushan. Lushan, in his carriage, cried out in shock: "What crime did my son commit that he was killed!"
translations.idiomatic: At Chenliu's outer gate Qingxu saw the notice of Qingzong's execution and wept to his father. Lushan, in his litter, wailed: "What crime did my son commit to be killed!"

sentences.zh: 狂而怒，官軍之降者夾道，命交相斫焉，死者六七千人，遂入陳留郡。

translations.literal: Maddened with rage, with surrendered government troops lining the road, he ordered them to hack one another to death; six or seven thousand died, and then he entered Chenliu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In a frenzy he had surrendered loyalists along the road cut one another down—six or seven thousand dead—then entered Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 太守郭納初拒戰，至是出降。

translations.literal: The prefect Guo Na had at first resisted; now he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Guo Na, who had resisted, now surrendered.

sentences.zh: 至滎陽，太守崔無詖拒戰，城陷死之。

translations.literal: At Xingyang, Prefect Cui Wubi resisted and died when the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingyang Prefect Cui Wubi fought to the death when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 次於泥水罌子谷，將軍荔非守瑜蹲而射之，殺數百人，矢及祿山輿。

translations.literal: They halted at Nishui Jar Valley. General Lifei Shouyu crouched and shot, killing several hundred; arrows reached Lushan's carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At Nishui Jar Valley General Lifei Shouyu knelt and shot, killing hundreds; arrows struck Lushan's litter.

sentences.zh: 祿山不敢過，乃取谷南而過。

translations.literal: Lushan dared not pass through and instead took the south side of the valley.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan dared not pass through and detoured south of the valley.

sentences.zh: 守瑜箭盡，投河而死。

translations.literal: When Shouyu's arrows were spent, he threw himself into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his arrows were gone, Shouyu threw himself into the river and died.

sentences.zh: 東京留守李悽、中丞盧奕、採訪使判官蔣清燒絕河陽橋。

translations.literal: Li Qi, acting eastern-capital intendant, Lu Yi the censor, and surveillance commissioner staff officer Jiang Qing burned the Heyang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Capital intendant Li Qi, censor Lu Yi, and staff officer Jiang Qing burned the Heyang Bridge.

sentences.zh: 祿山怒，率軍大至。

translations.literal: Lushan was enraged and led a great army up in force.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Lushan marched in force.

sentences.zh: 封常清自苑西隤牆，使伐樹塞路而奔。

translations.literal: Feng Changqing broke down the western garden wall, had trees felled to block the road, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Changqing breached the western palace wall, felled trees to block pursuit, and fled.

sentences.zh: 祿山入東京，殺李悽、盧奕、蔣清，召河南尹達奚珣，使之蒞事。

translations.literal: Lushan entered the Eastern Capital, killed Li Qi, Lu Yi, and Jiang Qing, and summoned Henan intendant Daxi Xun to take charge of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan entered Luoyang, executed Li Qi, Lu Yi, and Jiang Qing, and installed Henan intendant Daxi Xun to govern.

sentences.zh: 初，常清欲殺珣，恐應賊，悽、奕諫止之。

translations.literal: Earlier Feng Changqing had wished to kill Xun, fearing he would join the rebels; Li Qi and Lu Yi dissuaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Feng Changqing had wanted Xun killed lest he side with the rebels; Li Qi and Lu Yi had stopped him.

sentences.zh: 常清既敗，唯與數騎走至陝郡，高仙芝率兵守陝城，皆棄甲西走潼關，懼賊追躡，相蹂藉而死者塞路。

translations.literal: After Feng Changqing's defeat he fled with only a few horsemen to Shaan Commandery. Gao Xianzhi led troops to hold Shaan city, but all cast off their armor and fled west to Tong Pass; fearing pursuit by the rebels, they trampled one another and the dead choked the road.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, Feng fled with a handful of riders to Shaan; Gao Xianzhi held the city, but both armies shed armor and ran for Tong Pass, trampling one another until the road was choked with dead.

sentences.zh: 陝郡太守竇庭芝走投河東。

translations.literal: Shaan prefect Dou Tingzhi fled in distress to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Shaan prefect Dou Tingzhi fled east to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 賊使崔乾祐守陝郡。

translations.literal: The rebels sent Cui Qianyou to hold Shaan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels left Cui Qianyou to hold Shaan.

sentences.zh: 臨汝太守韋斌降於賊。

translations.literal: Linyu Prefect Wei Bin surrendered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Linyu prefect Wei Bin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，賊竊號燕國，立年聖武，達奚珣已下署為丞相，五月，南陽節度魯炅率荊、襄、黔中、嶺南子弟十萬餘，與賊將武令珣戰于葉縣城北枌河，王師盡沒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year the rebels usurped the title of Yan and established the era Shengwu; Daxi Xun and those below were appointed chancellors. In the fifth month Nanyang commissioner Lu Kui led more than one hundred thousand youths from Jing, Xiang, Qianzhong, and Lingnan and fought rebel general Wu Lingxun at the Fen River north of Yexian city; the imperial army was utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year they declared Yan and the era Shengwu, with Daxi Xun and others as chancellors. In the fifth month Lu Kui of Nanyang led a hundred thousand men from Jing, Xiang, Qianzhong, and Lingnan against Wu Lingxun at the Fen River north of Yexian; the imperial force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 六月，李光弼、郭子儀出土門路，大破賊眾於常山郡東嘉山，河北諸郡歸降者十餘。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi came out by the Tumen route and routed the rebel host east of Jia Mountain in Changshan Commandery; more than ten Hebei commanderies returned in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi marched out Tumen and shattered the rebels at Jia Mountain east of Changshan; more than ten Hebei districts submitted.

sentences.zh: 祿山窘急，圖欲卻投范陽。

translations.literal: Lushan was hard pressed and planned to withdraw to Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Lushan planned to fall back on Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 會哥舒翰自潼關領馬步八萬，與賊將崔乾祐戰於靈寶西，為賊覆敗，翰西奔潼關，為其帳下執送於賊。

translations.literal: Just then Ge Shuhan led eighty thousand horse and foot from Tong Pass and fought rebel general Cui Qianyou west of Lingbao; he was overwhelmed by the rebels. Han fled west to Tong Pass and was seized by his own subordinates and delivered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shuhan meanwhile led eighty thousand from Tong Pass against Cui Qianyou west of Lingbao, was routed, fled to Tong Pass, and was seized by his own men and handed to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 關門不守，玄宗幸蜀，太子收兵靈武。

translations.literal: The pass was not held; Xuanzong went in person to Shu, and the Crown Prince gathered troops at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: The pass fell; Xuanzong fled to Shu while the Crown Prince rallied troops at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 賊乃遣張通儒為西京留守，田乾真為京兆尹，安守忠屯兵苑中。

translations.literal: The rebels then sent Zhang Tongru as western-capital intendant, Tian Qianzhen as Jingzhao intendant, and An Shouzhong to encamp troops in the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: They posted Zhang Tongru as Luoyang intendant, Tian Qianzhen as Jingzhao governor, and An Shouzhong in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣阿史那承慶攻陷潁川，屠之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month they sent Ashina Chengqing to capture and sack Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Ashina Chengqing took Yingchuan and put it to the sword.

sentences.zh: 祿山以體肥，長帶瘡。

translations.literal: Because of his corpulence, Lushan constantly suffered from sores.
translations.idiomatic: His obesity left him chronically ulcerated.

sentences.zh: 及造逆後而眼漸昏，至是不見物。

translations.literal: After he rose in rebellion his eyes gradually dimmed; by this time he could see nothing.
translations.idiomatic: After his revolt his sight failed until he could see nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 又著疽疾。

translations.literal: He also developed a carbuncle.
translations.idiomatic: A carbuncle developed as well.

sentences.zh: 俄及至德二年正月朔受朝，瘡甚而中罷。

translations.literal: Soon, on the first day of the first month of the second year of Zhide, he held court; the sores were so severe that the audience was cut short midway.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of Zhide 2 he attempted court, but the pain was so great he broke off midway.

sentences.zh: 以疾加躁急，動用斧鉞。

translations.literal: His illness made him ever more irritable; he constantly resorted to axe and blade.
translations.idiomatic: Sickness fed his rage, and he killed at will with axe and sword.

sentences.zh: 嚴莊亦被捶撻，莊乃日夜謀之。

translations.literal: Yan Zhuang was also beaten; Zhuang then plotted day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang too was thrashed, and he plotted night and day.

sentences.zh: 立慶緒于戶外，莊持刀領豎李豬兒同入祿山帳內，豬兒以大刀斫其腹。

translations.literal: Qingxu was posted outside the door. Zhuang, knife in hand, led the eunuch Li Zhuer into Lushan's tent; Zhuer hacked open his belly with a great blade.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu stood guard outside while Zhuang led the eunuch Li Zhuer in with a knife; Zhuer slashed open Lushan's belly.

sentences.zh: 祿山眼無所見，床頭常有一刀，及覺難作，捫床頭不得，但撼幄帳大呼曰：「是我家賊！」

translations.literal: Lushan could see nothing. He always kept a knife at his bedside; when he sensed trouble and groped for it he could not find it, and could only shake the canopy and shout: "It is a traitor in my own house!"
translations.idiomatic: Blind, Lushan kept a knife by his bed; when he felt the attack and groped for it in vain, he shook the bed-curtains and roared, "A traitor in my own house!"

sentences.zh: 腹腸已數斗流在床上，言訖氣絕。

translations.literal: Several dou of entrails already streamed onto the bed; when he finished speaking his breath stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Entrails poured across the bed; he spoke once more and died.

sentences.zh: 因掘床下深數尺為坑，以氈罽包其屍埋之。

translations.literal: They dug a pit several chi deep beneath the bed, wrapped the corpse in felt and rugs, and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: They dug a pit beneath the bed, wrapped the body in felt, and buried it without ceremony.

sentences.zh: 又無哭泣之儀。

translations.literal: There was no mourning or weeping ritual.
translations.idiomatic: No mourning rites were observed.

sentences.zh: 莊即宣言於外，言祿山傳位於晉王慶緒，尊祿山為太上皇。

translations.literal: Zhuang immediately proclaimed abroad that Lushan had transmitted the throne to Prince of Jin Qingxu and honored Lushan as Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang announced that Lushan had abdicated to Prince Qingxu and taken the title Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 慶緒縱樂飲酒無度，呼莊為兄，事之大小必咨之。

translations.literal: Qingxu indulged in pleasure and drank without limit, called Zhuang "elder brother," and consulted him on every matter great or small.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu gave himself to revelry and drink, called Zhuang "brother," and consulted him on everything.

sentences.zh: 初，豬兒出契丹部落，十數歲事祿山，甚黠慧。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhuer had come from a Khitan tribe; in his teens he entered Lushan's service and was very clever.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuer came from a Khitan tribe and entered Lushan's service as a boy; he was exceptionally clever.

sentences.zh: 祿山持刃盡去其勢，血流數升，欲死，祿山以灰火傅之，盡日而蘇，因為閹人。

translations.literal: Lushan took a blade and completely removed his genitals; blood flowed several sheng and he nearly died. Lushan applied ash and fire to staunch it; by day's end he revived and thus became a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan castrated him with a knife; he lost several sheng of blood and nearly died. Lushan cauterized the wound with hot ash; by evening he lived, and became a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 祿山頗寵之，最見信用。

translations.literal: Lushan favored him greatly and trusted him most of all.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan doted on him and trusted him above all others.

sentences.zh: 祿山肚大，每著衣帶，三四人助之，兩人抬起肚，豬兒以頭戴之，始取裙褲帶及系腰帶。

translations.literal: Lushan's belly was enormous; whenever he dressed, three or four men assisted—two lifting his belly while Zhuer braced it with his head—before they could draw on skirt-trousers and fasten the belt.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan's belly was so vast that dressing required three or four men: two to lift the belly while Zhuer supported it with his head, then the garments and belt could be fastened.

sentences.zh: 玄宗寵祿山，賜華清宮湯浴，皆許豬兒等入助解著衣服，然終見刳者，豬兒也。

translations.literal: Xuanzong favored Lushan and granted him baths at Huaqing Palace; Zhuer and the others were allowed in to help him undress and dress. Yet in the end the one who disemboweled him was Zhuer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted Lushan baths at Huaqing and allowed Zhuer to attend him in undressing; yet it was Zhuer who finally gutted him.

sentences.zh: 慶緒，祿山第二子也。

translations.literal: Qingxu was Lushan's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu was Lushan's second son.

sentences.zh: 母康氏，祿山糟糠之妻。

translations.literal: His mother was Lady Kang, Lushan's wife of humble beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Kang, Lushan's wife from his days of poverty.

sentences.zh: 慶緒善騎射，祿山偏愛之。

translations.literal: Qingxu was skilled at riding and archery; Lushan favored him in particular.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in riding and archery, Qingxu was Lushan's favorite.

sentences.zh: 未二十，拜鴻臚卿，兼廣陽太守。

translations.literal: Before he was twenty he was appointed Minister of State Ceremonial and concurrent prefect of Guangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before twenty he was named Minister of State Ceremonial and prefect of Guangyang.

sentences.zh: 初名仁執，玄宗賜名慶緒，為祿山都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: His original name was Renzhi; Xuanzong granted the name Qingxu. He served as Lushan's director of all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Renzhi, he received the name Qingxu from the emperor and became Lushan's director of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 嚴莊、高尚立為偽主。

translations.literal: Yan Zhuang and Gao Shang installed him as the rebel sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang and Gao Shang made him rebel emperor.

sentences.zh: 慶緒素懦弱，言詞無序，莊恐眾不伏，不令見人。

translations.literal: Qingxu had always been weak and timid, his speech disorderly. Zhuang feared the troops would not submit and would not let him be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Timid and incoherent, Qingxu was kept from public view lest the army refuse him.

sentences.zh: 莊為偽御史大夫、馮翊郡王，以專其政。

translations.literal: Zhuang became rebel Censor-in-Chief and Prince of Fufeng, monopolizing government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang took the titles rebel Censor-in-Chief and Prince of Fufeng and ran the state himself.

sentences.zh: 厚其軍將官秩，以固其心。

translations.literal: He enriched the ranks and titles of the army officers to secure their loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He lavished rank on the generals to bind their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 二月，肅宗南幸鳳翔郡，始知祿山死，使僕固懷恩使於回紇，結婚請兵討逆。

translations.literal: In the second month Emperor Suzong went south in person to Fengxiang Commandery and first learned of Lushan's death. He sent Pugu Huai'en as envoy to the Uyghurs to contract a marriage alliance and request troops to suppress the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Suzong reached Fengxiang and learned Lushan was dead; he sent Pugu Huai'en to the Uyghurs for a marriage alliance and troops against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 其月，郭子儀拔河東郡，崔乾祐南遁。

translations.literal: That same month Guo Ziyi recovered Hedong Commandery and Cui Qianyou fled south.
translations.idiomatic: That month Guo Ziyi retook Hedong and Cui Qianyou fled south.

sentences.zh: 八月，回紇三千騎至。

translations.literal: In the eighth month three thousand Uyghur horsemen arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month three thousand Uyghur cavalry arrived.

sentences.zh: 九月，廣平王領蕃漢之眾收西京，走安守忠，賊之死者積如山阜。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Prince of Guangping led barbarian and Han forces to recover the Western Capital; An Shouzhong fled, and rebel dead piled like hills.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Prince of Guangping retook Chang'an with allied forces; An Shouzhong fled and rebel corpses heaped like hills.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊將尹子奇攻陷睢陽郡，殺張巡、姚摐等。

translations.literal: In the tenth month rebel general Yin Ziqi captured Suiyang Commandery and killed Zhang Xun, Yao Zong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yin Ziqi took Suiyang and killed Zhang Xun, Yao Zong, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 王師乘勝至陝郡，賊懼，令嚴莊傾其驍勇而來拒。

translations.literal: The imperial army pressed its advantage to Shaan Commandery. The rebels were afraid and ordered Yan Zhuang to bring all their elite troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army advanced to Shaan; the rebels in panic sent Yan Zhuang with every crack troop to hold them.

sentences.zh: 廣平王遣副元帥郭子儀等與賊戰于陝西曲沃，大破之於新店，逐北二十里，斬首十餘萬，伏屍三十里。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping sent deputy commander Guo Ziyi and others to fight the rebels at Quwo west of Shaan, routing them at Xindian, pursuing north twenty li, beheading more than one hundred thousand; corpses lay for thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi routed them at Quwo and Xindian, pursued twenty li, and left a hundred thousand dead over thirty li of road.

sentences.zh: 嚴莊奔至東京，告慶緒，慶緒率其餘眾奔河北，保鄴郡。

translations.literal: Yan Zhuang fled to the Eastern Capital and reported to Qingxu; Qingxu led his remaining troops to flee to Hebei and hold Ye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang fled to Luoyang to warn Qingxu, who retreated to Hebei and held Ye.

sentences.zh: 嚴莊至河內，南來歸順。

translations.literal: Yan Zhuang reached Henei and came south to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang reached Henei and surrendered to the court.

sentences.zh: 賊將阿史那承慶等麾下三萬餘人，悉奔恆、趙、范陽。

translations.literal: More than thirty thousand men under rebel generals Ashina Chengqing and others all fled to Heng, Zhao, and Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand under Ashina Chengqing and others scattered to Heng, Zhao, and Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 從慶緒者，唯疲卒一千三百而已。

translations.literal: Those who followed Qingxu were only thirteen hundred worn-out soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Only thirteen hundred exhausted men remained with Qingxu.

sentences.zh: 偽中書令張通儒秉政，改相州為成安府，署置百官。

translations.literal: The rebel Secretariat Director Zhang Tongru held power, changed Xiang Prefecture to Chengan Prefecture, and appointed the full roster of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tongru governed, renamed Xiang to Chengan, and installed a full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 旬日之內，賊將各以眾至者六萬餘，凶威復振。

translations.literal: Within ten days rebel generals arrived with their hosts totaling more than sixty thousand, and their fierce power revived.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days rebel commanders rallied sixty thousand men and their power revived.

sentences.zh: 偽青、齊節度能元皓獨率眾歸順，明年，改乾元元年，偽德州刺史王暕、貝州刺史宇文寬等皆歸順，河北諸軍各以城守累月，賊使蔡希德、安太清急擊，復陷於賊，虜之以歸，臠食其肉。

translations.literal: The rebel Qing and Qi commissioner Neng Yuanhao alone led his troops to submit. The next year, changed to the first year of Qianyuan, the rebel Dezhou prefect Wang Min, Beizhou prefect Yuwen Kuan, and others all submitted. Hebei armies held their cities for months; the rebels sent Cai Xide and An Taiqing in swift attack, recaptured them, took them captive back, and sliced their flesh to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Only Neng Yuanhao of Qing and Qi surrendered with his force. In Qianyuan 1 Wang Min of Dezhou, Yuwen Kuan of Beizhou, and others defected; but when Hebei garrisons held out for months, Cai Xide and An Taiqing stormed them back, carried off the defenders, and ate their flesh.

sentences.zh: 其下潛謀歸順者眾矣，賊皆易置之，以縱屠戮，人心始離。

translations.literal: Many among his subordinates secretly plotted to submit; the rebels treated them lightly and indulged in slaughter, and hearts began to turn away.
translations.idiomatic: Many subordinates plotted secretly to defect; the rebels answered with massacre, and loyalty began to crack.

sentences.zh: 又不親政事，繕治亭沼樓船，為長夜之飲。

translations.literal: He also did not attend to government affairs, but repaired pavilions, ponds, and tower-ships for all-night drinking.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored government, built pavilions and pleasure boats, and drank through the nights.

sentences.zh: 高尚等各不相葉。

translations.literal: Gao Shang and the others were all at odds with one another.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shang and the other ministers were at constant odds.

sentences.zh: 蔡希德兵最銳，性剛直，張通儒譖而縊殺之，三軍冤痛不為用。

translations.literal: Cai Xide's troops were the sharpest and he was upright by nature; Zhang Tongru slandered him and had him strangled. The whole army grieved in outrage and would not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xide commanded the finest troops and was blunt-spirited; Zhang Tongru slandered him to death by strangulation, and the army, bitter, would not fight.

sentences.zh: 以崔乾祐為天下兵馬使，權領中外兵。

translations.literal: Cui Qianyou was made commander of all armies under heaven, with authority over internal and external forces.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qianyou was named supreme commander with authority over all forces.

sentences.zh: 乾祐性愎戾，士卒不附。

translations.literal: Qianyou was obstinate and harsh by nature; the soldiers would not attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Obstinate and harsh, Qianyou won no loyalty from the ranks.

sentences.zh: 九月，肅宗遣郭子儀等九節度率步騎二十萬攻之，以魚朝恩為軍容使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Suzong sent Guo Ziyi and nine other commissioners with two hundred thousand foot and horse to attack him, appointing Yu Chao'en army superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Suzong sent Guo Ziyi and nine commissioners with two hundred thousand men against Ye, with Yu Chao'en as army superintendent.

sentences.zh: 初，子儀之列陳也，使善射者三千人伏於壘垣內。

translations.literal: At first, when Ziyi deployed his battle line, he had three thousand skilled archers lie in ambush within the ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyi formed his line, he hid three thousand archers inside the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 明日接戰，子儀麾其屬偽奔，慶緒逐之，伏者齊發，賊黨大潰。

translations.literal: The next day they joined battle; Ziyi ordered his men to feign flight and Qingxu pursued. The ambushers loosed together and the rebel host collapsed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Ziyi feigned retreat; Qingxu pursued into an ambush, and the rebel army broke.

sentences.zh: 使薛嵩求救于史思明，言禪讓之禮。

translations.literal: He sent Xue Song to beg Shi Siming for rescue, speaking of the rites of abdication and succession.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Song was sent to Shi Siming for aid, offering terms of abdication.

sentences.zh: 思明先遣李歸仁以步卒一萬、馬軍三千，先往滏陽以應。

translations.literal: Siming first sent Li Guiren with ten thousand foot and three thousand horse to Fuyang in advance as response.
translations.idiomatic: Siming first sent Li Guiren with ten thousand foot and three thousand horse to Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 及至滏陽，子儀之圍已固，築城穿壕各三重，樓櫓之盛，古所未有。

translations.literal: When they reached Fuyang, Ziyi's siege was already tight: walls and trenches threefold deep, watchtowers in such profusion as antiquity had never seen.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuyang they found Ziyi's siege complete—triple walls and trenches and watchtowers such as history had never seen.

sentences.zh: 又引水以灌城下，城中水泉大上，井皆滿溢。

translations.literal: They also diverted water to flood beneath the city; springs within rose high and every well overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: They flooded the ground below the city until springs and wells brimmed over inside.

sentences.zh: 以安太清代乾祐為都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: An Taiqing replaced Qianyou as director of all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An Taiqing replaced Qianyou as director of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 思明南攻魏州，節度使崔光遠南走，思明據其城數日，即乾元二年正月一日也。

translations.literal: Siming attacked Weizhou from the south; commissioner Cui Guangyuan fled south. Siming held the city for several days—this was the first day of the first month of the second year of Qianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Siming marched south on Weizhou; Cui Guangyuan fled, and Siming held the city for days—on New Year's Day of Qianyuan 2.

sentences.zh: 思明偽稱燕王，立年號。

translations.literal: Siming falsely styled himself King of Yan and established an era name.
translations.idiomatic: Siming declared himself King of Yan and took an era name.

sentences.zh: 慶緒自十月被圍至二月，城中人相食，米斗錢七萬餘，鼠一頭直數千，馬食隤牆麥鞬及馬糞濯而飼之。

translations.literal: From the tenth month when the siege began to the second month, people within the city ate one another; rice was more than seventy thousand cash per dou, a rat's head worth several thousand; horses ate fallen wall-grain and saddle stuffing, and even horse dung washed and fed to them.
translations.idiomatic: From the tenth month to the second, Ye starved: men ate men, grain cost seventy thousand per dou, a rat thousands; horses were fed rotten grain from the walls and washed dung.

sentences.zh: 思明引眾來救，三月六日，子儀等戰敗，遂解圍而南，斷河陽橋以守谷水。

translations.literal: Siming led his host to the rescue. On the sixth day of the third month Ziyi and the others were defeated, lifted the siege, and withdrew south, breaking the Heyang Bridge to hold the Gu River.
translations.idiomatic: Siming marched to relieve the city; on the sixth of the third month the imperial army was beaten, lifted the siege, burned Heyang Bridge, and held the Gu River line.

sentences.zh: 思明領其眾營于鄴縣南。

translations.literal: Siming led his troops to encamp south of Ye county.
translations.idiomatic: Siming camped south of Ye.

sentences.zh: 慶緒使收子儀等營中糧，尚六七萬石，復與孫孝哲、乾祐謀閉門自守，議更拒思明。

translations.literal: Qingxu had them gather grain from Ziyi's camps—still sixty or seventy thousand shi—and again plotted with Sun Xiaozhe and Qianyou to shut the gates and hold out, debating whether to resist Siming once more.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu seized sixty or seventy thousand shi from the imperial camps and with Sun Xiaozhe and Qianyou debated shutting the gates against Siming.

sentences.zh: 諸將曰「今日安可更背史王乎！」

translations.literal: The generals said: "How can we today turn our backs again on King Shi!"
translations.idiomatic: The generals cried: "How can we betray King Shi now!"

sentences.zh: 張通儒、高尚、平冽謂慶緒曰：「史王遠來，臣等皆合迎謝。」

translations.literal: Zhang Tongru, Gao Shang, and Ping Lie said to Qingxu: "King Shi has come from afar; we all ought to go out to welcome and thank him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tongru, Gao Shang, and Ping Lie urged: "King Shi has marched far to save us—we must go out to welcome him."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「任公暫往見思明。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Let Lord Ren go for now to see Siming."
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu answered: "Let Lord Ren go first to see Siming."

sentences.zh: 思明與之涕泗，厚其禮，復命歸城。

translations.literal: Siming wept with him, treated him with great courtesy, and sent him back to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Siming wept with him, honored him, and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 經三日，慶緒不至。

translations.literal: After three days Qingxu still did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Three days passed and Qingxu did not appear.

sentences.zh: 思明密召安太清令誘之。

translations.literal: Siming secretly summoned An Taiqing to lure him out.
translations.idiomatic: Siming secretly ordered An Taiqing to lure him out.

sentences.zh: 慶緒不獲已，以三百騎詣思明。

translations.literal: Qingxu had no choice; with three hundred horsemen he went to Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu, unable to refuse, rode out with three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 思明引入，令三軍擐甲執兵待之。

translations.literal: Siming brought him in and ordered the whole army to don armor and take up weapons awaiting him.
translations.idiomatic: Siming received him with the entire army armed and waiting.

sentences.zh: 及諸弟領至於庭，再拜稽首曰：「臣不克負荷，棄失兩都，久陷重圍，不意大王以太上皇故，將兵遠救。」

translations.literal: When he and his brothers were led into the courtyard, he bowed twice and touched his forehead to the ground, saying: "Your servant could not bear the burden, lost both capitals, and was long trapped in siege—I never expected that for the Retired Emperor's sake Your Majesty would lead troops from afar to rescue me."
translations.idiomatic: Brought with his brothers into the courtyard, he kowtowed: "I failed in my charge, lost both capitals, and was besieged so long—I never thought you would march so far for the Retired Emperor's sake."

sentences.zh: 思明曰：「棄失兩都，用兵不利，亦何事也！

translations.literal: Siming said: "Losing both capitals, military setbacks—what of it!
translations.idiomatic: Siming said: "Lost capitals, lost battles—what of that!

sentences.zh: 爾為人子，殺汝父以求位，庸非大逆乎？

translations.literal: You as a son killed your father to seize the throne—is this not the greatest treason?
translations.idiomatic: You murdered your father for the throne—is that not the greatest treason?

sentences.zh: 吾為太上皇討賊。」

translations.literal: I am punishing the traitor on behalf of the Retired Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: I punish the traitor for the Retired Emperor."

sentences.zh: 即牽出，並其四弟及高尚、孫孝哲、崔乾祐，皆縊殺之。

translations.literal: He was dragged out, and together with his four younger brothers and Gao Shang, Sun Xiaozhe, and Cui Qianyou—all were strangled.
translations.idiomatic: He was dragged out; his four brothers, Gao Shang, Sun Xiaozhe, and Cui Qianyou were all strangled with him.

sentences.zh: 祿山父子僭逆三年而滅。

translations.literal: Lushan father and son usurped for three years and then perished.
translations.idiomatic: The Lushans' rebellion lasted three years and ended in extinction.

sentences.zh: 初王師之圍相州也，意朝夕屠陷，唯術士桑道茂曰：「三月六日，西師必散，此城無憂。」

translations.literal: When the imperial army first besieged Xiangzhou, they expected to storm it any day; only the adept Sang Daomao said: "On the sixth day of the third month the western army will surely disperse; this city need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: When the siege began, the court expected instant victory; only the diviner Sang Daomao said: "On the sixth of the third month the western army will break—this city is safe."

sentences.zh: 卒如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it was exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: It came to pass exactly as he said.

sentences.zh: 高尚，幽州雍奴人也，本名不危。

translations.literal: Gao Shang was a man of Yongnu in Youzhou; his original name was Buwei.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shang came from Yongnu in Youzhou; he was born Buwei.

sentences.zh: 母老，乞食于人，尚周遊不歸侍養。

translations.literal: His mother was old and begged food from others; Shang wandered and did not return to care for her.
translations.idiomatic: His aged mother begged for food while he wandered and never came home to support her.

sentences.zh: 寓居河朔縣界，與令狐潮鄰里，通其婢，生一女，遂收之。

translations.literal: He lodged in the borderlands of Heshuo county, neighbor to Linghu Chao; he had relations with Chao's maidservant, who bore a daughter, and he took her in.
translations.idiomatic: Living on the Heshuo border near Linghu Chao, he lay with Chao's maid, who bore a daughter he then kept.

sentences.zh: 尚頗篤學，贍文詞。

translations.literal: Shang was quite devoted to learning and skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He studied hard and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 嘗歎息謂汝南周銑曰：「高不危寧當舉事而死，終不能咬草根以求活耳！」

translations.literal: He once sighed and said to Zhou Xian of Runan: "Gao Buwei would rather rise up and die in action than gnaw grass roots to stay alive!"
translations.idiomatic: He once told Zhou Xian of Runan: "I would rather die in rebellion than chew roots to survive!"

sentences.zh: 縣尉有姓高者，以其宗盟，引置門下，遂以尚入籍為兄弟。

translations.literal: A county lieutenant surnamed Gao, because of clan ties, took him into his household and entered Shang on the register as a brother.
translations.idiomatic: A county lieutenant named Gao, a clansman, took him in and registered him as a brother.

sentences.zh: 李齊物為懷州刺史，舉高尚不仕，送京師，並助錢三萬。

translations.literal: Li Qiwu was prefect of Huaizhou; he recommended Shang, who did not take office, and sent him to the capital, also providing thirty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiwu of Huaizhou recommended him; Shang declined office but was sent to the capital with thirty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 齊物寓書于中官將軍吳懷實以托之。

translations.literal: Qiwu sent a letter through the eunuch general Wu Huaishi to entrust him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiwu wrote the eunuch general Wu Huaishi to recommend him.

sentences.zh: 懷實引見高力士，置賓館中，令與男丞相錫為學，無問家事，一以委之。

translations.literal: Huaishi introduced him to Gao Lishi, lodged him in the guest house, and had him study with the male consort Cheng Xi; household matters were not asked—everything was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu presented him to Gao Lishi, housed him as a guest, and set him to study with Cheng Xi, leaving all household affairs in his hands.

sentences.zh: 無何，令妻父呂令皓特表薦之。

translations.literal: Before long, Lishi's father-in-law Lü Linghao memorialized specially to recommend him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lishi's father-in-law Lü Linghao memorialized to recommend him.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一年，祿山表為屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao, Lushan memorialized for him as Outer Gentleman of the Farms.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 11 Lushan had him named Outer Gentleman of the Farms.

sentences.zh: 及隨祿山寇陷東京，偽授中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When he followed Lushan in raiding and capturing the Eastern Capital, he was falsely appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan took Luoyang, he was made rebel Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 偽赦書制敕多出其手。

translations.literal: Most rebel amnesties, edicts, and ordinances came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Most rebel proclamations and edicts were drafted by him.

sentences.zh: 始，尚與嚴莊、孫孝哲計畫，白祿山以為事必成。

translations.literal: At the beginning Shang, with Yan Zhuang and Sun Xiaozhe, plotted and told Lushan the affair would surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At first he, Yan Zhuang, and Sun Xiaozhe assured Lushan the plot would succeed.

sentences.zh: 及顏杲卿殺李欽湊於土門，揚聲言榮王琬、哥舒翰二十萬眾徇河北，十七郡皆歸順。

translations.literal: When Yan Gaoqing killed Li Qintou at Tumen and spread word that Prince of Rong Wan and Ge Shuhan with two hundred thousand were marching through Hebei, seventeen commanderies all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Gaoqing killed Li Qintou at Tumen and rumors spread that Prince Wan and Ge Shuhan led two hundred thousand through Hebei, seventeen districts submitted.

sentences.zh: 顏真卿破袁知奉三萬眾於堂邑，賀蘭進明再拔信都，李光弼、郭子儀繼收常山、趙郡，河北路絕者再。

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing routed Yuan Zhiben's thirty thousand at Tangyi; Helan Jinming twice recovered Xindu; Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi successively retook Changshan and Zhao commanderies—the Hebei route was cut off again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing smashed Yuan Zhiben at Tangyi; Helan Jinming retook Xindu twice; Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi retook Changshan and Zhao—Hebei was severed again and again.

sentences.zh: 河南諸郡皆有防禦，潼關有哥舒翰之師。

translations.literal: All Henan commanderies had defenses; at Tong Pass was Ge Shuhan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Henan was defended everywhere, and Ge Shuhan held Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 祿山大懼，怒尚等曰：「汝元向我道萬全，必無所畏。

translations.literal: Lushan was greatly afraid and raged at Shang and the others: "You originally told me everything was secure and there was nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was terrified and raged: "You told me all was secure and I had nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 今四邊若此，賴鄭、汴數州尚存，向西至關，一步不通，河北並已無矣，萬全何在？

translations.literal: Now on all four sides it is like this; only a few prefectures such as Zheng and Bian still remain. Westward to the pass, not a step can get through; Hebei is already entirely gone—where is this 'complete security'?
translations.idiomatic: Now look—only Zheng and Bian remain; the road west to the pass is blocked; Hebei is gone—where is your security?

sentences.zh: 更不須見我。」

translations.literal: You need not see me again."
translations.idiomatic: Do not come before me again."

sentences.zh: 尚等遂數日不得見祿山，憂悶不知所為。

translations.literal: Shang and the others then could not see Lushan for days and were anxious and distressed, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: For days Shang and the rest could not see him and were desperate.

sentences.zh: 會田乾真自潼關至，曉諭祿山曰：「自古帝王，皆有勝敗，然後成大事，豈有一舉而得之者乎！

translations.literal: Just then Tian Qianzhen arrived from Tong Pass and admonished Lushan: "Since antiquity emperors have all had victories and defeats before accomplishing great deeds—who ever succeeded in a single stroke!
translations.idiomatic: Then Tian Qianzhen came from Tong Pass and reasoned with him: "Every emperor wins and loses before triumph—who succeeds at once!

sentences.zh: 今四邊兵馬雖多，皆非精銳，豈我之比。

translations.literal: Though troops on all four sides are many today, none are elite—how can they compare with us?
translations.idiomatic: The armies on every side are numerous but none are elite—how can they match us?

sentences.zh: 縱事不成，收取數萬眾，橫行天下，為一盜蹠，亦十年五歲矣，豈有人能制我耶！

translations.literal: Even if the affair does not succeed, gather tens of thousands of men, rampage across the realm, become a single Dao Zhi—still ten or five years! Is there anyone who could restrain me!
translations.idiomatic: Even if we fail, we can still rally tens of thousands, sweep the empire, and live like bandit-kings for a decade or more—who could stop us!

sentences.zh: 尚、莊等皆佐命元勳，何得隔絕不與相見，令其憂懼？

translations.literal: Shang, Zhuang, and the others are all founding meritorious ministers—how can you cut them off and refuse to see them, making them anxious and afraid?
translations.idiomatic: Shang, Zhuang, and the rest are your founding ministers—why shut them out and leave them in dread?

sentences.zh: 只此數人，豈不能為患乎？

translations.literal: Only these few men—could they not still cause trouble?
translations.idiomatic: A handful of men like that could still do you harm.

sentences.zh: 外間聞之，必心搖動。」

translations.literal: When those outside hear of it, their hearts will surely waver.
translations.idiomatic: Word will spread, and men's hearts will falter.

sentences.zh: 祿山喜曰：「阿浩，非汝誰能開豁我心裏事，今無憂矣！

translations.literal: Lushan said delightedly: "Ahao! Who but you could clear the troubles from my heart—now I am without worry!
translations.idiomatic: Lushan exclaimed with relief: "Ahao! Only you could lift this weight from my heart—now I have nothing to fear!

sentences.zh: 為之奈何？」

translations.literal: What is to be done about it?"
translations.idiomatic: What should we do?"

sentences.zh: 乾真曰：「不如喚取慰勞之。」

translations.literal: Qianzhen said: "It would be better to summon them and comfort them with rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhen replied: "Summon them and treat them warmly—that is best."

sentences.zh: 遂召尚等飲宴作樂，祿山自唱歌以送酒，待之如初。

translations.literal: So he summoned Shang and the others to drink, feast, and make music; Lushan himself sang to see them off with wine and treated them as at first.
translations.idiomatic: He called Shang and the others to a feast with music; Lushan sang to them himself as he passed the wine and received them as before.

sentences.zh: 阿浩，乾真小字也。

translations.literal: "Ahao" was Qianzhen's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: "Ahao" was Tian Qianzhen's courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 及慶緒至相州，偽授侍中。

translations.literal: When Qingxu reached Xiangzhou, [Qianzhen] was spuriously appointed Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingxu arrived at Xiangzhou, Qianzhen was given the rebel title of Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 孫孝哲，契丹人也。

translations.literal: Sun Xiaozhe was a Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiaozhe was a Khitan.

sentences.zh: 母為祿山所通，因得狎近。

translations.literal: His mother had been taken by Lushan as a lover, and through this he gained intimate access.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had taken his mother as a concubine, and through her the son won his confidence.

sentences.zh: 及祿山僭逆，偽授殿中監、閑廄使，封王。

translations.literal: When Lushan usurped, [Xiaozhe] was spuriously appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and Commissioner of the Imperial Stud, and enfeoffed as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, Xiaozhe was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and Commissioner of the Imperial Stud in the rebel regime, and enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 孝哲尤用事，亞于嚴莊。

translations.literal: Xiaozhe was especially influential, second only to Yan Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhe wielded great power, ranking just below Yan Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 裘馬華侈，頗事豪貴，每食皆備珍饌。

translations.literal: He favored splendid furs and horses and extravagant dress, often consorting with the great and powerful; every meal was set with rare delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in lavish style, kept company with the mighty, and never sat down to a meal without rare delicacies.

sentences.zh: 性殘忍，果于殺戮，聞者畏之。

translations.literal: By nature cruel, he was decisive in killing; those who heard of him feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Cruel by nature and swift to kill, he was widely feared.

sentences.zh: 祿山使孝哲與張通儒同守西京，妃王宗枝皆罹其酷。

translations.literal: Lushan sent Xiaozhe together with Zhang Tongru to defend the Western Capital; consorts, princes, and imperial clansmen all suffered his cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan put Xiaozhe and Zhang Tongru in charge of the Western Capital, where consorts, princes, and imperial kin all fell victim to his brutality.

sentences.zh: 與嚴莊爭權不睦。

translations.literal: He contended with Yan Zhuang for power and they were not on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yan Zhuang vied for power and were estranged.

sentences.zh: 及祿山死，奪其使，以鄧季陽代之。

translations.literal: When Lushan died, [Qingxu] took away his commission and replaced him with Deng Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Lushan died, Qingxu stripped him of his post and put Deng Jiyang in his place.

sentences.zh: 慶緒之奔，莊懼為所圖，因而來奔。

translations.literal: When Qingxu fled, Zhuang feared being plotted against and therefore came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingxu was in flight, Zhuang feared he would be targeted and defected to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 史思明，本名窣干。

translations.literal: Shi Siming—original name Sugan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming was originally named Sugan.

sentences.zh: 營州寧夷州突厥雜種胡人也。

translations.literal: A man of mixed Hu descent from Ningyi in Ying Prefecture—a Türk of mixed stock.
translations.idiomatic: He was a Türk of mixed descent from Ningyi in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 姿瘦，少鬚髮，鳶肩傴背，欽目側鼻。

translations.literal: He was gaunt, with little beard or hair; kite-like shoulders, hunched back; slanting eyes and a crooked nose.
translations.idiomatic: Gaunt and nearly beardless, he had stooped kite-shoulders, slanting eyes, and a crooked nose.

sentences.zh: 性急躁。

translations.literal: By nature he was irascible.
translations.idiomatic: He had a violent temper.

sentences.zh: 與安祿山同鄉里，先祿山一日生，思明除日生，祿山歲日生。

translations.literal: He was from the same village as An Lushan and was born one day before him—Siming on the day of chu, Lushan on the day of sui.
translations.idiomatic: He came from the same village as An Lushan and was born a day earlier, on the chu day of the calendar cycle; Lushan was born on the sui day.

sentences.zh: 及長，相善，俱以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: When they grew up, they were on good terms and both were famed for fierce valor.
translations.idiomatic: As adults they were close friends, both renowned for fierce courage.

sentences.zh: 初事特進烏知義，每令騎覘賊，必生擒以歸。

translations.literal: At first he served the Special Advance Wu Zhiyi; whenever sent on horseback to reconnoiter the enemy, he always captured them alive and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Wu Zhiyi, holder of the Special Advance title; sent to scout the enemy on horseback, he unfailingly brought captives back alive.

sentences.zh: 又解六蕃語，與祿山同為互市郎。

translations.literal: He also understood the six frontier languages and together with Lushan served as trade brokers.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke six frontier languages and, like Lushan, worked as a border-trade broker.

sentences.zh: 張守珪為幽州節度，奏為折沖。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shougui was military commissioner of Youzhou, he memorialized [to appoint Siming] as colonel of the crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shougui held Youzhou as military commissioner, he recommended Siming for appointment as a crack-troop colonel.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，頻立戰功，至將軍，知平盧軍事。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao era, he repeatedly achieved military merit, rose to General, and took charge of Pinglu military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianbao years he won repeated victories, rose to general, and took charge of Pinglu military affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘗入奏，玄宗賜坐，與語，甚奇之。

translations.literal: Once when he entered court to report, Xuanzong granted him a seat and spoke with him, and regarded him as remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: On one audience at court, Xuanzong gave him a seat, spoke with him, and was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 問其年，曰「四十矣」。

translations.literal: He asked his age. [Siming] said, "I am forty already."
translations.idiomatic: Asked his age, he answered, "Forty."

sentences.zh: 玄宗撫其背曰：「卿貴在後，勉之。」

translations.literal: Xuanzong stroked his back and said: "Your eminence lies ahead—exert yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong clapped him on the back and said, "Great honor awaits you—apply yourself.

sentences.zh: 遷大將軍、北平太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand General and Prefect of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand General and made Prefect of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 十一載，祿山奏授平盧節度都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Lushan memorialized that he be appointed chief military commissioner of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tianbao, Lushan recommended him as chief military commissioner of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 十四載，安祿山反，命思明討饒陽等諸郡，陷之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, An Lushan rebelled and ordered Siming to subdue Raoyang and other commanderies; they fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, An Lushan rebelled and sent Siming to conquer Raoyang and neighboring commanderies, which all fell.

sentences.zh: 十五載正月六日，思明與蔡希德圍顏杲卿於常山，九日拔之。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the first month of the fifteenth year, Siming together with Cai Xide besieged Yan Gaoqing at Changshan; on the ninth day they took it.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the first month of the fifteenth year, Siming and Cai Xide besieged Yan Gaoqing at Changshan and captured the city on the ninth.

sentences.zh: 又圍饒陽，二十九日不能拔。

translations.literal: He again besieged Raoyang; on the twenty-ninth day he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He then besieged Raoyang but failed to capture it even after twenty-nine days.

sentences.zh: 李光弼出土門，拔常山郡，思明解圍而拒光弼。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi came out through Tumen and recovered Changshan Commandery; Siming lifted the siege and blocked Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi marched out through Tumen, retook Changshan Commandery, and Siming broke off the siege to confront him.

sentences.zh: 光弼列兵于城南，相持累月。

translations.literal: Guangbi drew up his troops south of the city and they faced off for months.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi formed his line south of the city, and the two armies faced each other for months.

sentences.zh: 光弼草盡，使精卒以車數乘於旁縣取草，輒被擊之，其後率十匹唯共得兩束草，至剉蒿薦以飼之。

translations.literal: When Guangbi's fodder was exhausted, he sent elite soldiers in several carts to fetch grass in neighboring counties; they were always attacked. Thereafter on average only two bundles of grass were obtained from ten horses, and when they arrived they chopped reeds and straw to feed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangbi ran out of fodder, he sent picked men in carts to gather grass in nearby counties, but they were repeatedly ambushed; in the end ten horses had to share two bundles, and they fed the animals chopped reeds and straw.

sentences.zh: 初，祿山以賈循為范陽留後，謀歸順，為副留守向潤客所殺，以思明代之。

translations.literal: Initially, Lushan had appointed Jia Xun acting prefect of Fanyang; [Jia] planned to surrender but was killed by the deputy prefect Xiang Runke, and Siming was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: At first Lushan had made Jia Xun acting prefect of Fanyang; Jia plotted to surrender but was killed by the deputy prefect Xiang Runke, and Siming replaced him.

sentences.zh: 又以征戰在外，令向潤客代其任。

translations.literal: Because he was campaigning abroad, Lushan had Xiang Runke take over his duties.
translations.idiomatic: With Siming away on campaign, Lushan had Xiang Runke assume his responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 四月，朔方節度郭子儀以朔方蕃、漢二萬人自土門而至常山，軍威遂振，南拔趙郡，思明退保博陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, arrived at Changshan with twenty thousand Shuofang foreign and Han troops from Tumen; military prestige surged; they marched south and recovered Zhao Commandery; Siming withdrew to defend Boling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Guo Ziyi of Shuofang brought twenty thousand mixed foreign and Han troops through Tumen to Changshan; morale soared, Zhao Commandery was retaken to the south, and Siming fell back to Boling.

sentences.zh: 五月十日，子儀、光弼擊之，敗思明於沙河上。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the fifth month, Ziyi and Guangbi attacked him and defeated Siming on the Sha River.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth of the fifth month, Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi attacked and routed Siming on the Sha River.

sentences.zh: 又攻之，思明以騎卒奔嘉山，光弼擊之，思明大敗，走入博陵郡。

translations.literal: They attacked again; Siming fled with cavalry toward Jia Mountain; Guangbi struck him; Siming was utterly defeated and fled into Boling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Attacked again, Siming fled with his cavalry toward Jia Mountain; Guangbi pursued, crushed him, and drove him into Boling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 光弼圍之，城幾拔。

translations.literal: Guangbi besieged it; the city was nearly taken.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi besieged the city and nearly captured it.

sentences.zh: 屬潼關失守，肅宗理兵于朔方，使中官邢廷恩追朔方、河東兵馬。

translations.literal: At that time Tong Pass fell; Emperor Suzong organized troops at Shuofang and sent the eunuch Xing Yan'en to recall Shuofang and Hedong troops.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Tong Pass fell; Emperor Suzong gathered forces at Shuofang and sent the eunuch Xing Yan'en to recall the Shuofang and Hedong armies.

sentences.zh: 光弼入土門，思明隨後徼擊之。

translations.literal: Guangbi entered Tumen; Siming followed and attacked him from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi withdrew through Tumen, and Siming pursued and struck at his rear.

sentences.zh: 已而回軍並行擊劉正臣，正臣易之。

translations.literal: Soon after he turned his army and in parallel struck Liu Zhengchen; Zhengchen underestimated him.
translations.idiomatic: He then swung his army about and fell upon Liu Zhengchen, whom he took too lightly.

sentences.zh: 初不設備，遂棄軍保北平，正臣妻子及軍資二千乘盡沒。

translations.literal: At first unprepared, [Zhengchen] abandoned his army and withdrew to Beiping; Zhengchen's wife and children and two thousand cartloads of military supplies were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Caught unprepared, Zhengchen abandoned his army and fled to Beiping; his wife, children, and two thousand cartloads of supplies were all lost.

sentences.zh: 思明將卒頗精銳，皆平盧戰士，南拔常山、趙郡，又攻河間。

translations.literal: Siming's officers and soldiers were quite elite—all Pinglu warriors; they had marched south and taken Changshan and Zhao Commandery, and again attacked Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Siming's troops were crack Pinglu veterans; they had swept south through Changshan and Zhao Commandery and were now assaulting Hejian.

sentences.zh: 為尹子奇所圍，已四十餘日。

translations.literal: They were besieged by Yin Ziqi; already more than forty days had passed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi had them under siege for more than forty days.

sentences.zh: 顏真卿使和琳以一萬二千人、馬百匹以救之。

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing sent He Lin with twelve thousand men and a hundred horses to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing dispatched He Lin with twelve thousand men and a hundred horses to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 至河間二十餘里，北風勁烈，鼓聲不相聞，賊縱擊之，擒和琳以至城下。

translations.literal: When they reached within twenty-odd li of Hejian, a fierce north wind blew; drumbeats could not be heard; the rebels struck freely, captured He Lin, and brought him to the foot of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-odd li from Hejian a howling north wind drowned out the drums; the rebels charged, seized He Lin, and paraded him before the walls.

sentences.zh: 思明既全，合勢，賊軍益盛。

translations.literal: Siming having recovered intact, their combined force made the rebel army stronger still.
translations.idiomatic: Siming's force reunited intact, and the rebel army grew stronger than ever.

sentences.zh: 李奐為賊所擒，送東京。

translations.literal: Li Huan was captured by the rebels and sent to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan was taken prisoner and sent to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 又攻景城，擒李暐，暐投河而死。

translations.literal: They again attacked Jingcheng, captured Li Wei; Wei threw himself into a river and died.
translations.idiomatic: They next attacked Jingcheng, captured Li Wei, and Wei drowned himself in the river.

sentences.zh: 遂使康沒野波攻平原。

translations.literal: Then he sent Kang Moyabo to attack Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Kang Moyabo against Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 真卿覺之，兵馬既盡，渡河而南。

translations.literal: Zhenqing perceived it; his troops and horses were already exhausted; he crossed the river and went south.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing saw what was coming; his forces spent, he crossed the river and withdrew south.

sentences.zh: 攻清河，糧盡城陷，擒太守王懷忠以獻祿山。

translations.literal: They attacked Qinghe; when grain was exhausted the city fell; they captured Prefect Wang Huaizhong and presented him to Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: They took Qinghe when its grain ran out, seized Prefect Wang Huaizhong, and sent him to Lushan.

sentences.zh: 將軍莊嗣賢圍烏承恩於信都。

translations.literal: General Zhuang Sixian besieged Wu Cheng'en at Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: General Zhuang Sixian besieged Wu Cheng'en at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 承恩母、妻先為安祿山所獲，思明獲其男從則，使諭承恩，承恩遂降，思明與之把臂飲酒。

translations.literal: Cheng'en's mother and wife had already been captured by An Lushan; Siming captured his nephew Congze and sent him to urge Cheng'en to surrender; Cheng'en then submitted; Siming grasped his arm and drank with him.
