translations.idiomatic: Cheng'en's mother and wife were already in rebel hands; Siming captured his nephew Congze and sent him to negotiate; Cheng'en surrendered, and Siming clasped his arm and drank with him.

sentences.zh: 饒陽陷，李系投火死。

translations.literal: Raoyang fell; Li Xi threw himself into fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Raoyang fell, Li Xi burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 河北悉陷。

translations.literal: Hebei was entirely lost.
translations.idiomatic: All of Hebei was lost.

sentences.zh: 尹子奇以五萬眾渡河至青州，欲便向江、淮。

translations.literal: Yin Ziqi with fifty thousand men crossed the river to Qingzhou, intending to push straight toward the Yangtze and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi crossed the river to Qingzhou with fifty thousand men, aiming to drive straight toward the Yangtze and Huai.

sentences.zh: 會回紇二千騎奄至范陽，范陽閉門二日，然後向太原，子奇行千里以救之。

translations.literal: Just then two thousand Uyghur horsemen suddenly arrived at Fanyang; Fanyang closed its gates for two days, then [the Uyghurs] turned toward Taiyuan; Ziqi marched a thousand li to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Just then two thousand Uyghur horsemen suddenly appeared at Fanyang; the city shut its gates for two days before they turned toward Taiyuan, and Ziqi marched a thousand li to its relief.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，思明以蔡希德合范陽、上黨兵馬十萬，圍李光弼於太原。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Siming with Cai Xide combined Fanyang and Shangdang troops—a hundred thousand—and besieged Li Guangbi at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, Siming and Cai Xide joined a hundred thousand Fanyang and Shangdang troops to besiege Li Guangbi at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 光弼使為地道，至賊陣前。

translations.literal: Guangbi had them dig tunnels reaching in front of the rebel lines.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi had tunnels dug to emerge in front of the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 驍賊方戲弄城中人，地道中人出擒之。

translations.literal: While fierce rebels were disporting themselves mocking the city people, men from the tunnels emerged and seized them.
translations.idiomatic: While bold rebels were taunting the townspeople, men burst from the tunnels and grabbed them.

sentences.zh: 敵以為神，呼為「地藏菩薩」。

translations.literal: The enemy took it for the supernatural and called them "Earth Treasury Bodhisattvas."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels thought it supernatural and called them "Bodhisattvas of the Earth Treasury."

sentences.zh: 思明留十月，會安祿山死，慶緒令歸范陽，希德留百餘日，皆不能拔而歸。

translations.literal: Siming remained ten months; when An Lushan died, Qingxu ordered him back to Fanyang; Xide remained over a hundred days; neither could take [Taiyuan] and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Siming stayed ten months; when An Lushan died, Qingxu recalled him to Fanyang, while Xide lingered over a hundred days—neither could take the city and both withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自祿山陷兩京，常以駱駝運兩京禦府珍寶于范陽，不知紀極。

translations.literal: From the time Lushan seized the two capitals, he continually used camels to transport treasures from the imperial treasuries of the two capitals to Fanyang—beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: After Lushan took the two capitals, camel trains carried imperial treasures from both capitals to Fanyang in amounts beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 由是恣其逆謀。

translations.literal: By this Siming indulged his rebellious designs.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by this wealth, Siming gave free rein to his rebellious ambitions.

sentences.zh: 思明轉驕，不用慶緒之命。

translations.literal: Siming grew ever more arrogant and did not obey Qingxu's orders.
translations.idiomatic: Siming grew increasingly arrogant and ignored Qingxu's commands.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒為王師所敗，投鄴郡，其下蕃、漢兵三萬人，初不知所從，思明擊殺三千人，然後降之。

translations.literal: An Qingxu was defeated by the imperial armies and fled to Ye; his thirty thousand foreign and Han troops at first did not know whom to follow; Siming killed three thousand of them, and only then did they submit.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated by the imperial armies, An Qingxu fled to Ye; his thirty thousand foreign and Han soldiers did not know whom to serve until Siming slaughtered three thousand of them and forced the rest to submit.

sentences.zh: 慶緒使阿史那承慶、安守忠徵兵於思明，且欲圖之。

translations.literal: Qingxu sent Ashina Chengqing and An Shouzhong to summon troops from Siming and also intended to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu sent Ashina Chengqing and An Shouzhong to levy troops from Siming while plotting to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 判官耿仁智，忠謀之士，謂思明曰：「大夫崇重，人不敢言，仁智請一言而死。」

translations.literal: His judge Geng Renzhi, a man of loyal design, said to Siming: "Grand Marshal, you are greatly honored and men dare not speak; Renzhi asks to speak one word even if it costs his life.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Renzhi, his aide and a man of loyal counsel, said to Siming: "You stand so high that none dare speak plainly—I beg leave to speak one word, even at the cost of my life.

sentences.zh: 思明曰：「試言之。」

translations.literal: Siming said: "Try and speak."
translations.idiomatic: Siming said, "Speak, then."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「大夫久事祿山，祿山兵權若此，誰敢不服！

translations.literal: He replied: "Grand Marshal, you long served Lushan; when Lushan's military power was such as this, who dared not submit!
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "You served Lushan for years—when his power was at its height, who dared refuse him!

sentences.zh: 如大夫比者，逼於凶威耳，固亦無罪。

translations.literal: Men such as you, compelled by his fierce might, were likewise without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Men like you obeyed only under duress—you are not guilty of treason.

sentences.zh: 今聞孝感皇帝聰明勇智，有少康、周宣之略，大夫發使輸誠，必開懷見納，此轉禍為福之上策也。」

translations.literal: Now I hear that the Filial and Perspicacious Emperor is wise and courageous, with the strategic gifts of Shao Kang and King Xuan of Zhou; if the Grand Marshal sends envoys to offer loyalty, he will surely receive you openly—this is the supreme stratagem to turn disaster into blessing."
translations.idiomatic: The Filial and Perspicacious Emperor is said to be wise and bold, with the restoring genius of Shao Kang and King Xuan; send envoys to pledge loyalty and he will surely welcome you— that is the surest way to turn ruin into fortune."

sentences.zh: 思明曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Siming said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Siming said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 承慶等以五千騎至范陽，思明悉眾介胄以逆之。

translations.literal: Chengqing and the others arrived at Fanyang with five thousand horsemen; Siming led his entire host in armor to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing arrived at Fanyang with five thousand cavalry; Siming marched out in full armor with his entire army to meet them.

sentences.zh: 眾且數萬，去之一里，使謂之曰：「相公及王遠至，將士等不勝喜躍。

translations.literal: When the host numbered nearly ten thousand and was one li away, he had someone say to them: "The Prime Minister and the princes have arrived from afar; officers and soldiers cannot contain their joy.
translations.idiomatic: When his force of nearly ten thousand was still a li away, he sent word: "The Prime Minister and the princes have come from afar—the men can scarcely contain their joy.

sentences.zh: 此皆邊兵怯懦，頗懼相公之來，莫敢進也。

translations.literal: These are all frontier troops, timid and craven; they greatly fear the Prime Minister's coming and dare not advance.
translations.idiomatic: These frontier soldiers are timid and greatly fear your arrival—they dare not come forward.

sentences.zh: 請弛弓以安之。」

translations.literal: Pray loosen your bows to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Please unstring your bows to put them at ease.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: They complied.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed.

sentences.zh: 思明遂以承慶、守忠入內，飲樂之。

translations.literal: Siming then brought Chengqing and Shouzhong inside and entertained them with drink and music.
translations.idiomatic: Siming then ushered Chengqing and Shouzhong inside and feasted them with wine and music.

sentences.zh: 別令諸將於其所分收其甲仗。

translations.literal: Separately he ordered the various generals at their assigned stations to collect their armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile he ordered his generals at each station to seize their armor and arms.

sentences.zh: 其諸郡兵皆給糧，恣歸之，欲留者分隸諸營。

translations.literal: All the commandery troops were given provisions; those who wished to return were allowed to go; those who wished to remain were assigned to various camps.
translations.idiomatic: He rationed the commandery troops and let them go home if they wished; those who stayed were distributed among his camps.

sentences.zh: 遂拘承慶，斬守忠、李立節之首。

translations.literal: He then detained Chengqing and beheaded Shouzhong and Li Lijie.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Chengqing and beheaded Shouzhong and Li Lijie.

sentences.zh: 李光弼使衙官敬俛招之。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi sent his yamen officer Jing Mian to recruit him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi sent his staff officer Jing Mian to negotiate his surrender.

sentences.zh: 遂令衙官竇子昂奉表，以所管兵眾八萬人，及以偽河東節度高秀岩來降。

translations.literal: He then had his yamen officer Dou Zi'ang present a memorial, submitting the eighty thousand troops under his command together with the spurious Hedong commissioner Gao Xiuyan in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He had his staff officer Dou Zi'ang submit a memorial offering surrender with his eighty thousand troops and the rebel Hedong commissioner Gao Xiuyan.

sentences.zh: 肅宗大悅，封歸義王、范陽長史、御史大夫、河北節度使，朝義已下並為列卿，秀岩雲中太守，以其男如岳等七人為大官。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong was greatly pleased; he enfeoffed [Siming] as Prince of Returning Righteousness, Fanyang Chief Administrator, Censor-in-Chief, and Hebei Military Commissioner; Chaoyi and those below were all made chief ministers; Xiuyan was made Prefect of Yunzhong; his sons Ruyue and the other seven were given high offices.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong was delighted: he enfeoffed Siming as Prince of Returning Righteousness and made him Fanyang Chief Administrator, Censor-in-Chief, and Hebei Military Commissioner; Chaoyi and his other sons received court ranks; Xiuyan was made Prefect of Yunzhong; and Siming's seven sons, including Ruyue, were given high posts.

sentences.zh: 使內侍李思敬、將軍烏承恩宣慰使，令討殘賊。

translations.literal: He sent the palace eunuch Li Sijing and General Wu Cheng'en as envoy-commissioners to console them and order them to subdue the remaining rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched the eunuch Li Sijing and General Wu Cheng'en as commissioners to confirm the surrender and order them to crush the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 明年，改乾元元年，四月，肅宗使烏承恩為副使，候伺其過而殺之。

translations.literal: The next year, renamed the first year of Qianyuan; in the fourth month, Emperor Suzong sent Wu Cheng'en as deputy envoy to watch for his faults and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, the era was changed to Qianyuan; in the fourth month Emperor Suzong sent Wu Cheng'en back as deputy commissioner with orders to watch for an opening and assassinate Siming.

sentences.zh: 初，承恩父知義為節度，思明常事知義，亦有開獎之恩，以此李光弼冀其無疑，因謀殺之。

translations.literal: Initially, Cheng'en's father Zhiyi had been military commissioner; Siming had often served Zhiyi and had also received from him the grace of guidance and reward; for this reason Li Guangbi hoped he would not be suspected and plotted to kill Siming through this.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'en's father Zhiyi had once been military commissioner, and Siming had served under him and owed him patronage; Li Guangbi counted on that bond to keep Siming unsuspecting and planned the assassination accordingly.

sentences.zh: 承恩至范陽，數漏其情，夜取婦人衣衣之，詣諸將家，以翻動之意諭之。

translations.literal: When Cheng'en reached Fanyang, he repeatedly leaked the scheme; at night he put on women's clothes and visited the generals' houses, hinting at rebellion to them.
translations.idiomatic: At Fanyang, Cheng'en repeatedly betrayed the plot; by night he dressed in women's clothing, visited the generals' homes, and sounded them out about turning against Siming.

sentences.zh: 諸將以白思明，甚懼，無以為驗。

translations.literal: The generals all reported this to Siming; he was greatly afraid and had no way to verify it.
translations.idiomatic: The generals reported everything to Siming; terrified, he had no way to confirm or disprove what he heard.

sentences.zh: 有頃，承恩與思敬從上京來，宣恩命畢，將歸私第。

translations.literal: Before long, Cheng'en and Sijing came from the upper capital; when they had finished proclaiming the imperial grace, they were about to return to their private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, Wu Cheng'en and Li Sijing arrived from the capital; once they had delivered the emperor's commission, they prepared to return to their lodging.

sentences.zh: 思明留承恩且於館中，明當有所議。

translations.literal: Siming detained Cheng'en for the night in the guest house, saying that tomorrow there would be something to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Siming kept Cheng'en overnight at the guest house, saying they would confer the next day.

sentences.zh: 已令幃其所寢之床，伏二人於其下。

translations.literal: He had already ordered curtains hung around the bed where Cheng'en would sleep, with two men concealed beneath it.
translations.idiomatic: He had already curtained off Cheng'en's bed and hidden two men underneath.

sentences.zh: 承恩有小男，先留范陽，思明令省其父。

translations.literal: Cheng'en had a small son who had been left earlier at Fanyang; Siming had him visit his father.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'en's young son, who had been staying in Fanyang, was sent by Siming to see his father.

sentences.zh: 夜後，私於其子曰：「吾受命除此逆，明便授吾節度矣！」

translations.literal: After nightfall, Cheng'en spoke privately to his son, saying: "I have received orders to remove this rebel; tomorrow the military commission will be granted to me!
translations.idiomatic: That night Cheng'en spoke privately to his son: "I've been ordered to eliminate this traitor—tomorrow I'll be given the military commission!

sentences.zh: 床下二人叫呼而出，以告思明。

translations.literal: The two men beneath the bed cried out and emerged, reporting this to Siming.
translations.idiomatic: The two men under the bed shouted and burst forth to report what they had heard to Siming.

sentences.zh: 思明令執之，搜其衣曩，得朝廷所與阿史那承慶鐵券及光弼與承恩之牒，云：「承慶事了，即付鐵券；

translations.literal: Siming ordered him seized and searched the inside of his clothing, finding the iron tally the court had given Ashina Chengqing and a dispatch from Guangbi to Cheng'en, which said: "When Chengqing's affair is finished, then deliver the iron tally;
translations.idiomatic: Siming had Cheng'en arrested and searched his garments, finding the iron tally meant for Ashina Chengqing and a letter from Li Guangbi to Cheng'en reading: "Once the Chengqing matter is settled, hand over the iron tally;

sentences.zh: 不了，不可付之。」

translations.literal: If it is not finished, you must not deliver it.
translations.idiomatic: if not, do not hand it over.

sentences.zh: 又得簿書數百紙，皆載先所從反軍將名。

translations.literal: He also found several hundred sheets of registers, all recording the names of generals who had formerly followed the rebel army.
translations.idiomatic: He also found hundreds of pages of registers listing generals who had once served the rebels.

sentences.zh: 思明語之曰：「我何負於汝而至是耶？」

translations.literal: Siming said to him: "How have I wronged you that you would go this far?
translations.idiomatic: Siming demanded: "What wrong have I done you that you would come to this?

sentences.zh: 承恩稱：「死罪，此太尉光弼之謀也！」

translations.literal: Cheng'en declared: "This is a capital offense; this was Grand Marshal Guangbi's scheme!
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'en confessed: "I deserve death—it was Grand Marshal Li Guangbi's plot!

sentences.zh: 思明集軍將官吏百姓，西向大哭曰：「臣以十三州之地、十萬眾之兵降國家，赤心不負陛下，何至殺臣！」

translations.literal: Siming assembled military generals, officials, and common people, and facing west wept loudly, saying: "Your subject surrendered to the state with the land of thirteen prefectures and an army of a hundred thousand; with a loyal heart I have not failed Your Majesty—why would you kill your subject!
translations.idiomatic: Siming gathered his officers, officials, and townspeople and, facing west, wailed: "I surrendered thirteen prefectures and a hundred thousand men to the throne with a loyal heart—why would the emperor seek to kill me!

sentences.zh: 因搒殺承恩父子，囚李思敬，遣使表其事。

translations.literal: He then had Cheng'en and his son beaten and killed, imprisoned Li Sijing, and sent an envoy to memorialize the matter to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He had Cheng'en and his son beaten to death, imprisoned Li Sijing, and dispatched an envoy to report everything to the court.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又令中使慰諭云：「國家與光弼無此事，乃承恩所為，殺之善也。」

translations.literal: The court again sent a palace envoy to console and instruct him, saying: "The state and Guangbi had nothing to do with this; it was Cheng'en's doing—killing him was well done."
translations.idiomatic: The court sent another eunuch to reassure him: "The throne and Li Guangbi knew nothing of this—it was Cheng'en alone; you were right to kill him."

sentences.zh: 又有使從京至，執三司議罪人狀。

translations.literal: Another envoy arrived from the capital, bearing the roster of condemned criminals deliberated by the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Another messenger arrived from the capital carrying the Three Offices' list of condemned traitors.

sentences.zh: 思明曰：「陳希烈已下，皆重臣，上皇棄之幸蜀，既收復天下，此輩當慰勞之。

translations.literal: Siming said: "Chen Xilie and those below were all great ministers; the Retired Emperor abandoned them when he fled to Shu; now that the realm has been recovered, these men ought to be comforted and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Siming said: "Chen Xilie and the rest were senior ministers whom the Retired Emperor left behind when he fled to Shu—now that the empire is restored, they should be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 今尚見殺，況我本從祿山反乎！」

translations.literal: Yet now they are still being killed—how much more so for me, who originally followed Lushan in rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Yet they are being executed anyway—what hope is there for me, who once rebelled with An Lushan?

sentences.zh: 諸將皆云：「烏承恩之前事，情狀可知，光弼尚在，憂不細也。

translations.literal: All the generals said: "The circumstances of Wu Cheng'en's earlier affair are plain enough; as long as Guangbi remains, our worries are no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: The generals said: "Wu Cheng'en's case shows what awaits us—while Li Guangbi still holds command, our danger is grave.

sentences.zh: 大夫何不取諸將狀以誅光弼，以謝河北百姓！

translations.literal: Why does the Grand Marshal not gather the generals' petitions to execute Guangbi and appease the people of Hebei!
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal, why not petition with all the generals to execute Li Guangbi and answer to the people of Hebei?

sentences.zh: 主上若不惜光弼，為大夫誅之，大夫乃安；

translations.literal: If the sovereign is unwilling to sacrifice Guangbi and executes him for the Grand Marshal's sake, then the Grand Marshal will be secure;
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor will not spare Guangbi and executes him for you, you will be safe;

sentences.zh: 不然，為患未已。」

translations.literal: otherwise the troubles will not end.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise the threat will never pass.

sentences.zh: 思明曰：「公等言是。」

translations.literal: Siming said: "What you say is right."
translations.idiomatic: Siming agreed: "You are right."

sentences.zh: 乃令耿仁智、張不矜修表：「請誅光弼以謝河北。

translations.literal: He then ordered Geng Renzhi and Zhang Bujin to draft a memorial: "We request that Guangbi be executed to appease Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He had Geng Renzhi and Zhang Bujin draft a memorial asking that Li Guangbi be executed to satisfy Hebei.

sentences.zh: 若不從臣請，臣則自領兵往太原誅光弼。」

translations.literal: If you do not grant your subject's request, your subject will personally lead troops to Taiyuan to execute Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: If the throne refuses, I will lead my own army to Taiyuan and kill Guangbi myself.

sentences.zh: 不矜初以表示思明，及封入函，耿仁智盡削去之。

translations.literal: Bujin first presented the memorial to Siming; when it was sealed in its case, Geng Renzhi cut it all away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bujin showed the draft to Siming, but before sealing, Geng Renzhi stripped out the threatening passages.

sentences.zh: 寫表者密告思明，思明大怒，執二人於庭曰：「汝等何得負我？」

translations.literal: The memorial scribe secretly reported this to Siming; Siming was furious and seized the two men in the courtyard, saying: "How could you betray me?
translations.idiomatic: The clerk who copied the memorial tipped Siming off; enraged, Siming had both men brought into the courtyard and demanded: "How dare you betray me?

sentences.zh: 命斬之。

translations.literal: He ordered them beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered their execution.

sentences.zh: 仁智事思明頗久，意欲活之，卻令召入，謂之曰：「我任使汝向三十年，今日之事，我不負汝。」

translations.literal: Renzhi had served Siming for quite a long time; Siming, intending to spare him, had him summoned back in and said to him: "I have employed you for nearly thirty years; in today's matter I have not wronged you.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhi had served Siming for decades, and Siming meant to spare him; he had Renzhi called back and said: "I've relied on you for nearly thirty years—in today's affair I have not wronged you.

sentences.zh: 仁智大呼曰：「人生固有一死，須存忠節。

translations.literal: Renzhi shouted loudly: "Human life must end in death once; one must preserve loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhi cried out: "A man dies but once—it is better to keep faith and honor.

sentences.zh: 今大夫納邪說，為反逆之計，縱延旬月，不如早死，請速加斧鉞！」

translations.literal: Now the Grand Marshal has heeded wicked counsel and plots rebellion; even if I were to prolong my life for ten days or a month, it would be better to die early—I beg you quickly apply the axe!
translations.idiomatic: You take wicked counsel and rebel—I'd rather die now than linger a few more weeks; strike at once!

sentences.zh: 思明大怒，亂捶殺之，腦流於地。

translations.literal: Siming was enraged and beat him to death in a frenzy; his brains flowed upon the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Siming flew into a rage and beat him to death until his brains spilled on the ground.

sentences.zh: 十月，郭子儀領九節度圍相州，安慶緒偷道求救於思明，思明懼軍威之盛，不敢進。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Guo Ziyi at the head of nine military commissions besieged Xiangzhou; An Qingxu sent secretly by a side route to beg Siming for rescue; Siming, fearing the might of the imperial armies, did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Guo Ziyi led nine provincial armies in a siege of Xiangzhou; An Qingxu sent secretly for aid, but Siming, fearing the imperial host, did not dare march.

sentences.zh: 十二月，蕭華以魏州歸順，詔遣崔光遠替之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xiao Hua surrendered Weizhou to the court; an edict dispatched Cui Guangyuan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xiao Hua surrendered Weizhou; the court ordered Cui Guangyuan to take his place.

sentences.zh: 思明擊而拔其城，光遠脫身南渡。

translations.literal: Siming attacked and captured the city; Guangyuan escaped south across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Siming attacked, took the city, and Cui Guangyuan fled south across the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 思明于魏州殺三萬人，平地流血數日，既乾元二年正月一日也。

translations.literal: Siming at Weizhou killed thirty thousand people; the level ground flowed with blood for several days—this was already the first day of the first month of the second year of Qianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Weizhou Siming slaughtered thirty thousand; blood pooled for days—it was the first day of Qianyuan year two.

sentences.zh: 思明于魏州北設壇，僭稱為大聖燕王，以周贄為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Siming set up an altar north of Weizhou and arrogated to himself the title Great Sage King of Yan; he made Zhou Zan army marshal on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: North of Weizhou he raised an altar and proclaimed himself Great Sage King of Yan, appointing Zhou Zan his campaign marshal.

sentences.zh: 三月，引眾救相州，官軍敗而引退。

translations.literal: In the third month, he led his host to relieve Xiangzhou; the imperial armies were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he marched to relieve Xiangzhou and routed the imperial armies.

sentences.zh: 思明召慶緒等殺之，並有其眾。

translations.literal: Siming summoned Qingxu and the others and killed them, absorbing all their forces as well.
translations.idiomatic: Siming summoned An Qingxu and his followers and killed them, taking their armies into his own.

sentences.zh: 四月，僭稱大號，以周贄為相，以范陽為燕京。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, he arrogated the supreme imperial title, made Zhou Zan chancellor, and established Fanyang as Yen Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he proclaimed himself emperor, made Zhou Zan chancellor, and named Fanyang the Yan capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，寇汴州，節度使許叔冀合于思明，思明益振。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he raided Bianzhou; Military Commissioner Xu Shuji joined Siming, and Siming's strength increased further.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he struck at Bianzhou; when Xu Shuji, the military commissioner, defected to him, Siming's power surged.

sentences.zh: 又陷洛陽，與太尉光弼相拒。

translations.literal: He also captured Luoyang and confronted Grand Marshal Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Luoyang and faced off against Grand Marshal Li Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 思明恣行凶暴，下無聊矣！

translations.literal: Siming indulged in violent cruelty without restraint; those beneath him had no comfort left!
translations.idiomatic: Siming ruled with unrestrained cruelty; his subjects had no refuge.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，潛遣人反說官軍曰：「洛中將士，皆幽、朔人，咸思歸。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan, he secretly sent men to spread counter-propaganda among the imperial armies, saying: "The officers and soldiers at Luoyang are all men of You and Shuo; they all long to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan year two he secretly spread word among imperial troops: "The soldiers in Luoyang are all northerners who want to go home.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩以為然，告光弼及諸節度僕固懷恩、衛伯玉等：「可速出兵以討殘賊。」

translations.literal: Yu Chao'en believed this and told Guangbi and the various commissioners Pugu Huai'en, Wei Buyu, and others: "You should quickly send out troops to attack the remnant rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en believed it and urged Li Guangbi, Pugu Huai'en, Wei Buyu, and the other commissioners to march at once against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 光弼等然之，乃出師兩道齊進。

translations.literal: Guangbi and the others agreed; they then marched out by two routes advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi and the others agreed and advanced on two converging columns.

sentences.zh: 次榆林，賊委物偽遁，將士等不復設備，皆入城虜掠。

translations.literal: When they halted at Yulin, the rebels abandoned goods and feigned retreat; the officers and soldiers no longer maintained guard and all entered the city to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: At Yulin the rebels abandoned supplies and pretended to flee; the imperial troops dropped their guard and rushed into town to loot.

sentences.zh: 賊伏兵在北邙山下，因大下，士卒咸棄甲奔散。

translations.literal: Rebel troops lay in ambush at the foot of Mount Beimang; they then descended in force, and the soldiers all cast off their armor and fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel ambushers on Mount Beimang swept down; the soldiers threw off their armor and scattered.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩、衛伯玉退保陝州，光弼、懷恩棄河陽城，退居聞喜。

translations.literal: Yu Chao'en and Wei Buyu withdrew to defend Shanzhou; Guangbi and Huai'en abandoned Heyang city and withdrew to Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en and Wei Buyu fell back on Shanzhou; Li Guangbi and Pugu Huai'en abandoned Heyang and retreated to Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 步兵散死者數千人，軍資器械盡為賊所有，河陽、懷州盡陷於賊。

translations.literal: Several thousand foot soldiers were killed in the rout; all military supplies and equipment fell to the rebels; Heyang and Huaizhou were entirely lost to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of infantry died in the rout; the rebels took all supplies and arms; Heyang and Huaizhou fell entirely.

sentences.zh: 思明至陝州，為官軍所拒于姜子阪，戰不利，退歸永寧。

translations.literal: Siming reached Shanzhou and was blocked by the imperial armies at Jiangzi Slope; the battle went poorly and he withdrew to Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Siming reached Shanzhou but was stopped at Jiangzi Slope; defeated, he fell back to Yongning.

sentences.zh: 築三角城，約一月內畢，以貯軍糧。

translations.literal: He built Triangular Fortress, planning to finish it within about one month, to store military grain.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Triangular Fortress built, to be finished within a month, as a granary.

sentences.zh: 朝義築城畢，未泥，思明至，詬之。

translations.literal: Chaoyi finished building the fortress but had not yet plastered it; Siming arrived and reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi completed the walls but had not yet plastered them when Siming came and berated him.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「緣兵士疲乏，暫歇耳！」

translations.literal: [Chaoyi] replied: "Because the soldiers were exhausted, we paused for a rest!
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi answered: "The men were exhausted—we've only paused to rest!

sentences.zh: 又怒曰：「汝惜部下兵，違我處分。」

translations.literal: Siming again said angrily: "You spare your subordinate soldiers and disobey my orders.
translations.idiomatic: Siming raged: "You coddle your own troops and defy my orders.

sentences.zh: 令隨身數十人立馬看泥，斯須而畢。

translations.literal: He ordered several dozen of his personal attendants to stand by their horses and watch the plastering; in an instant it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: He had a few dozen attendants stand over the men on horseback while they plastered; in moments the work was done.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「待收陝州，斬卻此賊。」

translations.literal: He also said: "When Shanzhou is taken, I will behead this villain.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Once Shanzhou is mine, I'll cut off this wretch's head.

sentences.zh: 朝義大懼。

translations.literal: Chaoyi was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi was terrified.

sentences.zh: 思明居驛，朝義在店中。

translations.literal: Siming lodged at the relay station; Chaoyi stayed at an inn.
translations.idiomatic: Siming stayed at the post station; Chaoyi at a nearby inn.

sentences.zh: 思明令腹心曹將軍總中軍兵嚴衛，朝義將駱悅並許叔冀男季常等言：「主上欲害王，悅與王死無日矣！」

translations.literal: Siming ordered his trusted follower General Cao to command the central army in strict guard; Chaoyi's general Luo Yue together with Xu Shuji's son Jichang and others said: "The sovereign intends to harm the Prince; you and the Prince, Yue, will not live long!
translations.idiomatic: Siming put his confidant General Cao in charge of the central guard; Chaoyi's general Luo Yue and Xu Shuji's son Jichang said to him: "The emperor means to kill you—we'll all be dead before long!

sentences.zh: 因言：「廢興之事，古來有之，欲喚取曹將軍舉大事，可乎？」

translations.literal: They then said: "Matters of deposition and enthronement have existed since antiquity; we wish to summon General Cao to undertake the great affair—would that be acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: They added: "Kings have been overthrown before—shall we bring in General Cao and do what must be done?"

sentences.zh: 朝義回面不應。

translations.literal: Chaoyi turned his face away and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi looked away and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「若不應，悅等即歸李家，王亦不全矣！」

translations.literal: Yue said: "If you do not consent, we will at once return to the Li family; you, Prince, will not remain whole either!
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yue warned: "If you refuse, we go over to the Tang—and you won't survive either!

sentences.zh: 朝義然之，令許季常命曹將軍至。

translations.literal: Chaoyi agreed; he had Xu Jichang summon General Cao to come.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi assented and sent Xu Jichang to fetch General Cao.

sentences.zh: 悅等告之，不敢拒。

translations.literal: Yue and the others told him [the plan]; he did not dare refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yue laid out the plot; Cao dared not refuse.

sentences.zh: 其夜，思明夢而驚悟，據床惆悵。

translations.literal: That night Siming started awake from a dream, leaned on his bed in melancholy distress.
translations.idiomatic: That night Siming jolted awake from a dream and sat on his bed in dread.

sentences.zh: 每好伶人，寢食置左右，以其殘忍，皆恨之。

translations.literal: He had always favored entertainers and kept them at his side during sleep and meals; because of his cruelty, they all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Siming kept actors at his side day and night; they all hated his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 及此，問其故，曰：「吾向夢見水中沙上群鹿渡水而至，鹿死水乾。」

translations.literal: On this occasion he asked them the reason; he said: "I just dreamed that on sand in water a herd of deer crossed the water and came; the deer died and the water dried up.
translations.idiomatic: He asked what troubled him and said: "I dreamed of deer crossing water onto a sandbank—the deer died and the water ran dry.

sentences.zh: 言畢如廁。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking he went to the privy.
translations.idiomatic: Having said this, he went to relieve himself.

sentences.zh: 伶人相謂曰：「鹿者，祿也；

translations.literal: The entertainers said to one another: "Deer means emolument and office;
translations.idiomatic: The actors whispered among themselves: "Deer means rank and fortune;

sentences.zh: 水者，命也。

translations.literal: water means life.
translations.idiomatic: water means life.

sentences.zh: 胡祿命俱盡矣！」

translations.literal: The barbarian's emolument and life are both exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian's fortune and life are spent!

sentences.zh: 駱悅入，問思明所在，未及對，殺數人，因指在廁。

translations.literal: Luo Yue entered and asked where Siming was; before anyone could answer, he killed several people; someone then pointed to [him] being in the privy.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yue burst in asking where Siming was; before anyone could answer he killed several men; someone pointed toward the privy.

sentences.zh: 思明覺變，逾牆出，至馬槽，備馬騎之。

translations.literal: Siming sensed the mutiny, climbed over the wall and went out, reached the horse trough, prepared a horse and mounted it.
translations.idiomatic: Siming sensed treachery, vaulted the wall, saddled a horse at the trough, and rode off.

sentences.zh: 悅等至，令傔人周子俊射，中其臂，落馬。

translations.literal: When Yue and the others arrived, he ordered his attendant Zhou Zijun to shoot; the arrow struck Siming's arm and he fell from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yue ordered his servant Zhou Zijun to shoot; an arrow struck Siming's arm and he fell from his horse.

sentences.zh: 曰：「是何事？」

translations.literal: Siming said: "What is this about?
translations.idiomatic: Siming cried: "What's happening?

sentences.zh: 悅等告以懷王。

translations.literal: Yue and the others told him it was on behalf of Prince Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yue said it was Prince Huai's doing.

sentences.zh: 思明曰：「我朝來語錯，今有此事。

translations.literal: Siming said: "My words this morning were wrong; now this has happened.
translations.idiomatic: Siming said: "I spoke rashly this morning—and now this.

sentences.zh: 然汝殺我太疾，何不待我收長安？

translations.literal: Yet you kill me too quickly—why not wait until I have recovered Chang'an?
translations.idiomatic: But you move too fast—why not wait until I retake Chang'an?

sentences.zh: 終事不成矣！」

translations.literal: In the end the enterprise will not succeed!
translations.idiomatic: You've ruined everything!

sentences.zh: 因急呼懷王者三，曰：「莫殺我！」

translations.literal: He then urgently called out "Prince Huai!" three times, saying: "Do not kill me!
translations.idiomatic: He cried "Prince Huai!" three times: "Don't kill me!"

sentences.zh: 卻罵曹將軍曰：「這胡誤我，這胡誤我！」

translations.literal: He then cursed General Cao, saying: "This barbarian misled me, this barbarian misled me!
translations.idiomatic: Then he cursed General Cao: "That fool ruined me—that fool ruined me!"

sentences.zh: 悅遂令心腹擒思明赴柳泉驛，曰：「事已成矣！」

translations.literal: Yue then ordered his trusted men to seize Siming and take him to Liuchuan Post, saying: "The affair is accomplished!
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yue's men dragged Siming to Liuchuan Post and announced: "It's done!"

sentences.zh: 朝義曰：「莫驚聖人否？

translations.literal: Chaoyi said: "Was the Sage not alarmed?
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi asked: "Did you frighten the Emperor?

sentences.zh: 莫損聖人否？」

translations.literal: Was the Sage not harmed?
translations.idiomatic: Was he hurt?

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「無有。」

translations.literal: Yue said: "There was none."
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yue said: "No."

sentences.zh: 時周贄、許叔冀統後軍在福昌，朝義令許季常往告之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou Zan and Xu Shuji commanded the rear army at Fuchang; Chaoyi sent Xu Jichang to inform them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zan and Xu Shuji held the rear at Fuchang; Chaoyi sent Xu Jichang to tell them.

sentences.zh: 贄聞，驚欲仰倒。

translations.literal: When Zan heard, he was so startled he nearly fell backward.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zan was so shocked he nearly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 朝義卻領兵回，贄等來迎，因殺贄。

translations.literal: Chaoyi then led his troops back; when Zan and the others came to meet him, he killed Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi marched back; when Zhou Zan came out to meet him, Chaoyi killed him.

sentences.zh: 思明至柳泉驛，縊殺之。

translations.literal: When Siming reached Liuchuan Post, they strangled him to death.
translations.idiomatic: At Liuchuan Post they strangled Siming.

sentences.zh: 朝義便僭偽位。

translations.literal: Chaoyi at once usurped the false throne.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi seized the rebel throne.

sentences.zh: 朝義，思明孽子也。

translations.literal: Chaoyi was Siming's illegitimate son.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyi was Siming's bastard son.

sentences.zh: 寬厚，人附之，使人往范陽，殺偽太子朝英等。

translations.literal: He was generous and mild; people attached themselves to him; he sent men to Fanyang to kill the false crown prince Chaoying and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Mild and generous, he won men's loyalty; he sent agents to Fanyang to kill the rebel crown prince Chaoying and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 偽留守張通儒覺之，戰於城中。

translations.literal: The false garrison commander Zhang Tongru detected them and fought in the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan garrison commander Zhang Tongru discovered the plot and battle erupted in the city.

sentences.zh: 數日，死者數千人，始斬之。

translations.literal: After several days, several thousand were dead; only then was [Tongru] beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: After several days and thousands dead, Zhang Tongru was finally killed.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽四面數百里，人相食，州縣為墟。

translations.literal: At that time, for several hundred li on every side of Luoyang, people ate one another; prefectures and counties became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: For hundreds of miles around Luoyang men ate one another; towns lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 諸節度使皆祿山舊將，與思明等夷，朝義徵召不至。

translations.literal: The various military commissioners were all old generals of Lushan, treated the same as Siming and the others; when Chaoyi summoned them, they did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial commanders were all veterans of An Lushan's army, peers of Siming; none answered Chaoyi's summons.

sentences.zh: 思明乾元二年僭號，至朝義寶應元年滅，凡四年。

translations.literal: From the time Siming usurped the imperial title in the second year of Qianyuan until Chaoyi's destruction in the first year of Baoying, altogether four years.
translations.idiomatic: From Siming's usurpation in Qianyuan year two to Chaoyi's fall in Baoying year one—four years in all.
